title.zh: 卷一百四十二 列傳第六十七 李楊崔柳韋路
title.raw: 卷一百四十二 列傳第六十七 李楊崔柳韋路 Volume 142 Biographies 67:

sentences.zh: 李楊崔柳韋路

translations.literal: Li, Yang, Cui, Liu, Wei, Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Li, Yang, Cui, Liu, Wei, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 李麟，裔出懿祖，於屬最疏。

translations.literal: Li Lin, a descendant issuing from Emperor Yizong, was among the most distant in the lineage.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lin traced his descent from Emperor Yizong and stood among the most remote branches of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 父濬，歷潤、虢、潞三州刺史，以誠信號良吏。

translations.literal: His father Jun successively served as prefect of Run, Guo, and Lu, and was styled a good official for sincerity and trust.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jun served in turn as prefect of Run, Guo, and Lu, and was renowned as an upright official for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 開元中，終劍南節度按察使，贈戶部尚書，謚曰誠。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era he ended as military commissioner and inspection commissioner of Jiannan; posthumously he was given Minister of Revenue, posthumous name Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he ended his career as military commissioner and inspection commissioner of Jiannan; posthumously he was made Minister of Revenue with the posthumous name Cheng (Sincere).

sentences.zh: 麟好學，善文辭。

translations.literal: Lin loved learning and was skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was devoted to learning and excelled at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 以父蔭補京兆府戶曹參軍，舉宗室異能，轉殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he was appointed household-registration staff officer in the Jingzhao prefectural office; recommended for exceptional ability among the imperial clan, he was transferred to palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he entered service as a household-registration aide in the Jingzhao prefectural office; recommended for exceptional talent among imperial clansmen, he was promoted to palace censor.

sentences.zh: 累擢兵部侍郎，與楊國忠同列，國忠怙權，疾之，改權禮部貢舉。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War; serving in the same rank as Yang Guozhong, Guozhong relied on power, resented him, and had him changed to oversee the Ministry of Rites examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Vice Minister of War; he served alongside Yang Guozhong, who, relying on his power, took offense at him and had him reassigned to oversee the Ministry of Rites examinations.

sentences.zh: 國忠遷，麟復本官。

translations.literal: When Guozhong was transferred, Lin resumed his original office.
translations.idiomatic: When Guozhong was transferred away, Lin returned to his former post.

sentences.zh: 改國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was changed to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 出為河東太守，有清政。

translations.literal: Sent out as prefect of Hedong, he had pure administration.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as prefect of Hedong, he governed with notable integrity.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，朝廷以麟儒者，非禦侮才，還為祭酒，封渭源縣男。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, the court considered Lin a Confucian scholar, not talent for repelling insult, and recalled him as Chancellor of Education, enfeoffing him as Baron of Weiyuan County.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rebelled, the court judged Lin a scholar rather than a man fit to repel invasion, recalled him as Chancellor of Education, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Weiyuan County.

sentences.zh: 玄宗入蜀，麟走見帝，再遷憲部尚書、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong entered Shu, Lin hurried to see the emperor and was twice promoted—to Minister of Justice and Associate Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong fled into Shu, Lin rushed to join him and was twice promoted—to Minister of Justice and Associate Councilor.

sentences.zh: 時宰相韋見素、房琯、崔渙、崔圓踵赴肅宗行在，獨麟以宗室子留總百司。

translations.literal: At that time chief ministers Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, Cui Huan, and Cui Yuan followed one after another to Emperor Suzong's traveling court; only Lin, as an imperial clansman, remained to oversee all offices.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the chief ministers Wei Jiansu, Fang Guan, Cui Huan, and Cui Yuan followed one after another to Emperor Suzong's mobile court; only Lin, as a member of the imperial clan, stayed behind to oversee all government offices.

sentences.zh: 上皇還京，進同中書門下三品，封褒國公。

translations.literal: When the Retired Emperor returned to the capital, Lin was advanced to Third Rank Associate Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Retired Emperor returned to Chang'an, Lin was promoted to Third Rank Associate Councilor and enfeoffed as Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 張皇后挾李輔國浸橈政，苗晉卿、崔圓等畏其權，皆附離取安，獨麟守正不阿順，輔國忌恚。

translations.literal: Empress Zhang, relying on Li Fuguo, gradually encroached on government; Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, and others feared his power and all kept their distance to secure safety; only Lin upheld rectitude without flattering compliance, and Fuguo resented him in hatred.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang, leaning on Li Fuguo, gradually encroached on government; Miao Jinqing, Cui Yuan, and others feared his power and kept their distance to stay safe; only Lin held to rectitude without currying favor, and Fuguo came to hate him.

sentences.zh: 乾元初，罷為太子少傅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianyuan he was dismissed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Qianyuan era he was removed and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年卒，年六十六，贈太子太傅，謚曰德。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged sixty-six; posthumously he was given Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name De.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at sixty-six; posthumously he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous name De (Virtuous).

sentences.zh: 楊綰，字公權，華州華陰人。

translations.literal: Yang Guan, courtesy name Gongquan, was a man of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Guan, courtesy name Gongquan, was a native of Huayin in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖溫玉，在武后時為顯官。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wenyu was a prominent official in Empress Wu's time.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wenyu had been a prominent official under Empress Wu.

sentences.zh: 世以儒聞。

translations.literal: The family was famed for Confucian learning through generations.
translations.idiomatic: The family had been renowned for Confucian learning for generations.

sentences.zh: 綰少孤，家素貧，事母謹甚。

translations.literal: Guan was orphaned young; the household had always been poor, and he served his mother with great care.
translations.idiomatic: Guan lost his father early; his family had long been poor, and he attended his mother with scrupulous devotion.

sentences.zh: 性沈靖，獨處一室，左右圖史，凝塵滿席，淡如也。

translations.literal: By nature he was calm and quiet; dwelling alone in one room, with histories and maps at hand, settled dust covered the mats—he was indifferent to it all.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was reserved and tranquil; he lived alone in one room, histories and maps at hand, dust thick on the mats, and remained utterly indifferent to such things.

sentences.zh: 不好立名，有所論著，未始示人。

translations.literal: He did not like to make a name for himself; whatever he wrote he never showed to others.
translations.idiomatic: He cared little for reputation; whatever he wrote he never showed to anyone.

sentences.zh: 第進士，補太子正字。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed proofreader to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 舉詞藻宏麗科，玄宗已試，又加詩、賦各一篇，綰為冠，由是擢右拾遣。

translations.literal: He entered the examination for magnificent diction; after Emperor Xuanzong had already tested them, he added one poem and one fu each—Guan took first place and was thereby promoted to Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the examination for magnificent literary style; after the emperor had already tested the candidates, he added one poem and one fu apiece—Guan ranked first and was promoted to Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 制舉加詩、賦，繇綰始。

translations.literal: Adding poetry and fu to the special examinations began with Guan.
translations.idiomatic: The addition of poetry and fu to the special examinations began with Guan.

sentences.zh: 天寶亂，肅宗即位，綰脫身見行朝，拜起居舍人，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao turmoil, when Emperor Suzong took the throne, Guan escaped to join the traveling court and was appointed Master of Documents and charged with drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao upheaval, when Emperor Suzong took the throne, Guan made his way to the mobile court and was appointed Master of Documents with charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter and concurrently edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Secretariat Drafter and concurrently edited the national history.

sentences.zh: 故事，舍人年久者為閣老，其公廨雜料獨取五之四。

translations.literal: By precedent, the drafter of longest tenure was called Pavilion Elder and alone took four-fifths of the office's miscellaneous supplies.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the senior drafter was called Pavilion Elder and alone claimed four-fifths of the office's miscellaneous supplies.

sentences.zh: 至綰，悉均給之。

translations.literal: When it came to Guan, he distributed them all equally.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan took office, he divided everything equally among them.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部侍郎，建復古孝廉、力田等科，天下高其議。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Minister of Rites and established the restored ancient examinations for Filial and Incorrupt and for Strength in Farming, among others; the realm honored his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Minister of Rites he revived the ancient examinations for Filial and Incorrupt candidates and for Strength in Farming, among others, and scholars throughout the empire praised his proposals.

sentences.zh: 俄遷吏部，品裁清允，人服其公。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; his judgments of rank were clear and fair, and people submitted to his impartiality.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was moved to the Ministry of Personnel; his assessments were clear and fair, and people respected his impartiality.

sentences.zh: 是時，元載秉政，忌綰望高，疏薄之。

translations.literal: At that time Yuan Zai held power, resented Guan's high standing, and kept him at a distance.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yuan Zai held power, envied Guan's high standing, and treated him coldly.

sentences.zh: 宦者魚朝恩判國子監，既誅，因是建言太學當得天下名儒汰其選，即拜綰國子祭酒，外示尊重，而實以散地處之。

translations.literal: The eunuch Yu Chaoen had supervised the Directorate of Education; once he was executed, on this basis it was proposed that the Imperial Academy should have famous scholars throughout the realm to sift its selections—Guan was immediately appointed Chancellor of the Directorate, outwardly showing respect while in fact placing him in a post without real power.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yu Chaoen had overseen the Directorate of Education; after he was executed, it was proposed that the Imperial Academy should be staffed with renowned scholars from across the realm to refine its selections—Guan was promptly made Chancellor of the Directorate, a show of respect that in fact parked him in a post without real authority.

sentences.zh: 載日貪冒，天下士議益歸綰，帝亦知之，自擢為太常卿，充禮儀使。

translations.literal: Zai grew daily more greedy; scholarly opinion throughout the realm increasingly turned to Guan, and the emperor knew it too, personally promoting him to Minister of Ceremonies and making him Commissioner of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zai grew ever more corrupt; scholarly opinion across the empire increasingly favored Guan, and the emperor knew it, personally promoting him to Minister of Ceremonies and appointing him Commissioner of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 載得罪，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，修國史。

translations.literal: When Zai was found guilty, Guan was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Councilor, and edited the national history.
translations.idiomatic: When Zai fell from power, Guan was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Councilor and continued to edit the national history.

sentences.zh: 制下，士相賀於朝，綰固讓，帝不許。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, scholars congratulated one another at court; Guan firmly declined, but the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, scholars congratulated one another at court; Guan firmly declined, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 時諸州悉帶團練使，綰奏：「刺史自有持節諸軍事以掌軍旅；

translations.literal: At that time all prefectures carried regimentation commissioners; Guan memorialized: "Prefects already have the authority of holding the tally over all military affairs to command armies;
translations.idiomatic: At that time every prefecture had a regimentation commissioner; Guan memorialized: "Prefects already hold the authority of commander-in-chief over military affairs;

sentences.zh: 司馬，古司武，所以副軍，今副使；

translations.literal: the prefectural marshal, anciently overseer of military affairs, was meant to assist the army—today's deputy commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: the prefectural marshal, in antiquity the overseer of military affairs, was meant to assist the army—the present deputy commissioner;

sentences.zh: 司兵參軍，即今團練判官。

translations.literal: the military staff officer is today's regimentation judge.
translations.idiomatic: the military staff officer is today's regimentation adjutant.

sentences.zh: 官號重復，可罷天下團練、守捉使。」

translations.literal: office titles are duplicated—regimentation and garrison commissioners throughout the realm may be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: The titles duplicate one another—regimentation and garrison commissioners throughout the realm should be abolished."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又減諸道觀察判官員之半。

translations.literal: He also reduced observation-commission adjutants in each circuit by half.
translations.idiomatic: He also cut the adjutants of circuit observation commissioners by half.

sentences.zh: 復言：「舊制，刺史被代若別追，皆降魚書，乃得去。

translations.literal: He further said: "Under the old system, when a prefect was replaced or separately summoned, fish tally documents were issued before he could depart.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Under the old system, when a prefect was replaced or separately summoned, fish tally documents had to be issued before he could leave office.

sentences.zh: 開元時，置諸道采訪使，得專停刺史，威柄外移，漸不可久。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era circuit investigation commissioners were established and could on their own halt prefects—authority shifted outward and could not long continue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era circuit investigation commissioners were created with power to suspend prefects on their own authority—power had shifted outward and could not be sustained indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 其刺史不稱職若贓負，本道使具條以聞，不得擅追及停，而刺史亦不得輒去州詣使所。

translations.literal: If a prefect was unfit for office or guilty of embezzlement, the circuit commissioner was to set out the particulars in a report and might not on his own summon or suspend him; nor might the prefect leave the prefecture on his own to go to the commissioner's office.
translations.idiomatic: If a prefect was incompetent or guilty of corruption, the circuit commissioner was to report the particulars and might not on his own summon or suspend him; nor might the prefect leave the prefecture on his own to visit the commissioner's office.

sentences.zh: 如其故闕，使司無署攝，聽上佐代領。」

translations.literal: If the old office fell vacant, and the commissioner's office had no acting appointment on file, the senior aide might be allowed to take charge."
translations.idiomatic: If the post fell vacant and the commissioner's office had filed no acting appointment, the senior aide might be allowed to take charge."

sentences.zh: 帝善其謀，於是高選州上佐，定上、中、下州，差置兵員，詔郎官、御史分道巡覆。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his plan; thereupon senior prefectural aides were chosen with care, upper, middle, and lower prefectures were fixed, military quotas were differentially set, and an edict ordered palace officials and censors to tour and review by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan; thereupon senior prefectural aides were chosen with care, upper, middle, and lower prefectures were classified, troop quotas were set accordingly, and an edict ordered palace officials and censors to tour and review the circuits by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 又定府、州官月稟，使優狹相均。

translations.literal: He also fixed the monthly allowances of prefectural and district officials so that prosperous and poor posts would be equalized.
translations.idiomatic: He also standardized the monthly allowances of prefectural and district officials so that prosperous and poor posts would be balanced.

sentences.zh: 始，天下兵興，從權宜，官品同而祿例差。

translations.literal: At first, when warfare arose throughout the realm, expedients were followed—ranks were the same but salary scales differed.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when warfare spread across the realm, expedients were followed—ranks were the same but salary scales varied widely.

sentences.zh: 及四方粗定，元載、王縉當國，偷以為利，因不改，故江淮大州至月千緡，而山劍貧險，雖上州刺史止數十緡。

translations.literal: When the four quarters were roughly settled, Yuan Zai and Wang Jin held power and secretly took this as profit, and therefore did not change it—so great prefectures of the Jiang-Huai received up to a thousand strings a month, while in the poor and perilous mountains of Shu even upper-grade prefects received only a few dozen strings.
translations.idiomatic: When the empire was roughly pacified, Yuan Zai and Wang Jin held power and quietly profited from the disparity, and therefore left it unchanged—so wealthy Jiang-Huai prefectures received up to a thousand strings a month, while in the poor and rugged Shu region even upper-grade prefects received only a few dozen strings.

sentences.zh: 及此始復太平舊制。

translations.literal: Only now was the old system of the Taiping era restored.
translations.idiomatic: Only now was the old Taiping-era system restored.

sentences.zh: 綰素痼疾，居旬日浸劇，有詔就中書療治，每對延英殿，許挾扶。

translations.literal: Guan had long suffered a chronic illness; within ten days it grew worse; an edict ordered treatment at the Secretariat, and whenever he faced audience in the Hall of Prolonged Brilliance he was permitted support on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Guan had long suffered a chronic illness; within ten days it grew worse; an edict ordered that he be treated at the Secretariat, and whenever he attended audience in the Hall of Prolonged Brilliance he was allowed to be supported on either side.

sentences.zh: 於時厘補穿敝，唯綰是恃。

translations.literal: At that time, in sorting out and mending what was torn and worn, only Guan was relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, in sorting out and repairing what was torn and worn, the court relied on Guan alone.

sentences.zh: 未幾薨，帝驚悼，詔群臣曰：「天不使朕致太平，何奪綰之速邪？」

translations.literal: Before long he died; the emperor was startled and grieved and told the assembled ministers: "Heaven does not let Us bring peace—why take Guan so swiftly?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died; the emperor was shocked and grieved and told the assembled ministers: "Heaven will not let Us bring peace—why take Guan so soon?"

sentences.zh: 即日詔贈司徒，遣使者冊授，欲及其未斂也。

translations.literal: That same day an edict posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor; envoys were sent to invest him by patent, wishing to reach him before encoffinment.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor; envoys were sent to invest him by patent, hoping to reach him before the body was encoffined.

sentences.zh: 詔百官如第吊，遣使會吊，賻絹千匹、布三百匹。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to mourn at his residence; envoys were sent to join in mourning, with condolence gifts of a thousand bolts of silk and three hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered all officials to mourn at his residence; envoys were sent to join in the mourning, with condolence gifts of a thousand bolts of silk and three hundred bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 太常謚曰文貞，比部郎中蘇端，憸人也，持異議，宰相常袞陰助之，帝以其言醜險不實，貶端巴州員外司馬，猶賜謚曰文簡。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous name Wen Zhen; Su Duan, bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue, a crafty man, held a dissenting view; Chief Minister Chang Gun secretly aided him; the emperor judged his words ugly, insidious, and untrue and demoted Duan to acting prefectural marshal in Ba Prefecture, yet still granted the posthumous name Wen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Ceremonies proposed the posthumous name Wen Zhen (Cultivated and Upright); Su Duan, a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and a crafty man, dissented; Chief Minister Chang Gun secretly backed him; the emperor judged his words malicious and false and demoted Duan to acting prefectural marshal in Ba Prefecture, yet still granted the posthumous name Wen Jian (Cultivated and Simple).

sentences.zh: 綰儉約，未嘗問生事，祿稟分姻舊，隨多寡輒盡。

translations.literal: Guan was frugal; he never inquired into livelihood; his salary he divided among kin and old friends, and however much or little there was he spent it all.
translations.idiomatic: Guan lived frugally and never troubled himself about livelihood; he divided his salary among kin and old friends and spent whatever he had to the last.

sentences.zh: 造之者，清談終晷，而不及榮利，欲幹以私，聞其言，必內愧止。

translations.literal: Those who visited him found pure conversation through the day without mention of glory or profit; those who wished to press private requests, hearing his words, invariably stopped inwardly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Visitors found him engaged in pure conversation through the day without a word of rank or profit; anyone who came hoping to press a private request, hearing him speak, invariably withdrew inwardly ashamed.

sentences.zh: 經誥微趣，學家疑晦者，一見既詣其極。

translations.literal: Subtle points in the classics and edicts that scholars found obscure—at one meeting he reached their utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Subtle points in the classics and edicts that scholars found obscure—at a single meeting he would reach their heart.

sentences.zh: 始輔政，御史中丞崔寬本豪侈，城南別墅池觀堂皇，為當時第一，即日遣人毀之；

translations.literal: When he first entered auxiliary government, Censor-in-Chief Cui Kuan had been extravagant; his suburban villa south of the city, with pools and towers grand and bright, was first in the age—that very day Guan sent men to destroy it;
translations.idiomatic: When he first took office as chief minister, Censor-in-Chief Cui Kuan had been extravagant; his suburban villa south of the city, with pools and halls magnificent beyond any of the day, was destroyed that very day on Guan's orders;

sentences.zh: 京兆尹黎幹，出入從騶馭百數，省損才留十餘騎；

translations.literal: Jingzhao Intendant Li Gan, going in and out with more than a hundred mounted attendants, had them reduced until only a dozen or so riders remained;
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhao Intendant Li Gan, who went abroad with more than a hundred mounted attendants, was ordered to keep only a dozen or so riders;

sentences.zh: 中書令郭子儀在邠州行營，方大會，除書至，音樂散五之四；

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Guo Ziyi was at the field headquarters in Bin Prefecture, just holding a great assembly—when the appointment notice arrived, four-fifths of the musicians dispersed;
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Guo Ziyi was at the field headquarters in Bin Prefecture, just holding a great banquet—when word of the appointment arrived, four-fifths of the musicians were dismissed;

sentences.zh: 它聞風靡然自化者，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: others who heard the wind and were transformed of themselves cannot be fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: others who took the cue and reformed themselves cannot be fully counted.

sentences.zh: 世以比楊震、山濤、謝安雲。

translations.literal: The age compared him to Yang Zhen, Shan Tao, and Xie An.
translations.idiomatic: His contemporaries compared him to Yang Zhen, Shan Tao, and Xie An.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫，字貽孫，太子賓客孝公沔之子也。

translations.literal: Cui Youfu, courtesy name Yisun, was son of the Heir Apparent's Mentor, the Duke of Xiao, Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Youfu, courtesy name Yisun, was the son of the Heir Apparent's Mentor, Duke Xiao of Mian.

sentences.zh: 世以禮法為聞家。

translations.literal: For generations the family was famed for ritual and law.
translations.idiomatic: For generations the family had been renowned for ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調壽安尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed sheriff of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed sheriff of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 安祿山陷洛陽，祐甫冒矢石入私廟，負木主以逃。

translations.literal: When An Lushan took Luoyang, Youfu braved arrows and stones to enter the private ancestral temple and fled carrying the spirit tablet.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan seized Luoyang, Youfu braved arrows and stones to enter the family ancestral temple and fled carrying the spirit tablet.

sentences.zh: 自起居舍人累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: From Master of Documents he was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: From Master of Documents he rose repeatedly to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，遇事不回。

translations.literal: By nature he was firm and upright; in affairs he did not bend.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was firm and upright and would not bend in a dispute.

sentences.zh: 時侍郎闕，祐甫攝省事，數與宰相常袞爭議不平。

translations.literal: When the vice directorship was vacant, Youfu handled affairs in its stead and several times disputed with Chief Minister Chang Gun without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the vice directorship was vacant, Youfu handled its affairs and repeatedly clashed with Chief Minister Chang Gun without yielding.

sentences.zh: 袞怒，使知吏部選，每擬官，袞輒駁異，祐甫不為下。

translations.literal: Gun grew angry and had him put in charge of personnel selection; whenever Youfu proposed an appointment, Gun would reject it with objections, and Youfu would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Gun grew angry and put him in charge of personnel selection; whenever Youfu proposed an appointment, Gun would object, and Youfu would not back down.

sentences.zh: 會朱泚軍中貓鼠同乳，表其瑞，詔示袞，袞率群臣賀，祐甫獨曰：「可吊不可賀。」

translations.literal: It happened that in Zhu Ci's army a cat and a rat nursed together; this was reported as an auspicious sign; an edict showed it to Gun, and Gun led the ministers in congratulation—Youfu alone said: "One may mourn but not congratulate."
translations.idiomatic: It happened that in Zhu Ci's army a cat and a rat nursed together; this was reported as an auspicious omen; an edict showed it to Gun, who led the ministers in congratulation—Youfu alone said: "This calls for mourning, not congratulation."

sentences.zh: 詔使問狀，對曰：「臣聞《禮》：『迎貓，為其食田鼠。』

translations.literal: An edict envoy asked the reason; he replied: "Your servant has heard in the Rites: 'Welcoming the cat is because it eats field mice.
translations.idiomatic: An edict envoy asked his reasoning; he replied: "Your servant has read in the Rites: 'Welcoming the cat is because it eats field mice.

sentences.zh: 以其為人去害，雖細必錄。

translations.literal: Because it removes harm for people, even small things must be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Because it removes harm for people—even small matters must be recorded.

sentences.zh: 今貓受畜於人，不能食鼠而反乳之，無乃失其性邪？

translations.literal: Now the cat is kept by men, cannot eat mice yet instead nurses them—has it not lost its nature?
translations.idiomatic: Now the cat is kept by men, cannot eat mice, yet nurses them instead—has it not lost its nature?

sentences.zh: 貓職不修，其應若曰法吏有不觸邪，疆吏有不捍敵。

translations.literal: The cat's duty is not fulfilled; the corresponding sign is as if legal officers do not touch evil, and frontier officers do not repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The cat's duty is unfulfilled; the corresponding sign is as if legal officers do not touch evil and frontier officers do not repel the enemy.

sentences.zh: 臣愚以為當命有司察貪吏，誡邊候，勤僥巡，則貓能致功，鼠不為害。」

translations.literal: Your servant foolishly thinks the authorities should be ordered to investigate greedy officials, warn the frontier posts, and diligently conduct patrols—then the cat can achieve its work and mice will not be harmful."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes the authorities should be ordered to investigate corrupt officials, warn the frontier posts, and conduct diligent patrols—then the cat can do its work and mice will not be harmful."

sentences.zh: 代宗異其言，袞益不喜。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong found his words unusual; Gun disliked him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong was struck by his words; Gun disliked him all the more.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，袞與禮官議：「禮，為君斬衰三年。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Gun discussed with the ritual officers: "By ritual, for a ruler one wears the severest mourning for three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Gun discussed with the ritual officers: "By ritual, mourning for a ruler requires the severest grade for three years.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝權制三十六日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han by expedient rule set thirty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han by expedient rule set thirty-six days.

sentences.zh: 我太宗文皇帝崩，遺詔亦三十六日，群臣不忍，既葬而除，略盡四月。

translations.literal: When Our Taizong the Cultivated Emperor died, the testamentary edict also set thirty-six days; the ministers could not bear it and, after burial, removed mourning—roughly four months in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Our Taizong the Cultivated Emperor died, the testamentary edict also set thirty-six days; the ministers could not bear it and, after burial, removed mourning—roughly four months in all.

sentences.zh: 高宗如漢故事。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong followed the Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong followed the Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 玄宗以來，始變天子喪為二十七日。

translations.literal: From Emperor Xuanzong onward, the Son of Heaven's mourning was first changed to twenty-seven days.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Xuanzong onward, the Son of Heaven's mourning was first shortened to twenty-seven days.

sentences.zh: 乃者，遺詔雖曰『天下吏民，三日釋服』，群臣宜如皇帝服二十七日乃除。」

translations.literal: Recently, although the testamentary edict said 'Officials and commoners throughout the realm, release mourning in three days,' the assembled ministers ought, like the emperor, to wear mourning twenty-seven days before removing it."
translations.idiomatic: Recently, although the testamentary edict said 'Officials and commoners throughout the realm, release mourning in three days,' the assembled ministers ought, like the emperor, to wear mourning twenty-seven days before removing it."

sentences.zh: 祐甫曰：「遺詔無臣、庶人之別，是皇帝宜二十七日，而群臣三日也。」

translations.literal: Youfu said: "The testamentary edict makes no distinction between ministers and commoners—the emperor ought to observe twenty-seven days, while the assembled ministers three days."
translations.idiomatic: Youfu said: "The testamentary edict makes no distinction between ministers and commoners—the emperor ought to observe twenty-seven days, while the assembled ministers three days."

sentences.zh: 袞曰：「賀循稱，吏者，官長所署，非公卿百官也。」

translations.literal: Gun said: "He Xun said that li means those appointed by office heads, not the public ministers and hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: Gun said: "He Xun said that li refers to those appointed by office heads, not the public ministers and hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 祐甫對：「《傳曰》『委之三吏』，乃三公也。

translations.literal: Youfu replied: "The Commentary says 'entrust to the three li'—these are the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu replied: "The Commentary says 'entrust to the three li'—these are the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 史稱循吏、良吏，豈胥吏歟？」

translations.literal: Histories speak of orderly officials and good officials—are these petty clerks?"
translations.idiomatic: Histories speak of orderly officials and good officials—are these petty clerks?"

sentences.zh: 袞曰：「禮非天降地出，人情而已。

translations.literal: Gun said: "Ritual does not fall from heaven or rise from earth—it is human feeling alone.
translations.idiomatic: Gun said: "Ritual does not fall from heaven or rise from earth—it is human feeling alone.

sentences.zh: 且公卿在臣膺受寵祿，今與黔首同，信宿而除，於公安乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, as ministers the dukes and secretaries receive favor and stipends; now to be the same as the black-headed people and remove mourning after one or two nights—how is that secure for the gentlemen?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as ministers the dukes and secretaries receive favor and stipends; now to be treated like commoners and shed mourning after a night or two—how can that be fitting for gentlemen?"

sentences.zh: 祐甫曰：「若遺詔何？

translations.literal: Youfu said: "What of the testamentary edict then?
translations.idiomatic: Youfu said: "What of the testamentary edict then?

sentences.zh: 詔而可改，孰不可改？」

translations.literal: If an edict may be changed, what may not be changed?"
translations.idiomatic: If an edict may be changed, what may not be changed?"

sentences.zh: 意象殊厲。

translations.literal: His bearing and intent were exceptionally stern.
translations.idiomatic: His bearing and intent were exceptionally stern.

sentences.zh: 袞方入臨，遣從吏扶立殿墀上，祐甫指之謂眾曰：「臣哭君前，有扶禮乎？」

translations.literal: Gun was just entering to mourn; he sent attendant clerks to support him standing on the hall terrace—Youfu pointed at them and said to the assembly: "When a minister weeps before his ruler, is there ritual for supporting him?"
translations.idiomatic: Gun was just entering to mourn; he sent attendant clerks to support him standing on the hall terrace—Youfu pointed at them and said to the assembly: "When a minister weeps before his ruler, is there ritual for supporting him?"

sentences.zh: 袞不勝怒，乃劾祐甫率情變禮，橈國典，請貶潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Gun could not contain his anger and memorialized that Youfu followed personal feeling to alter ritual, bent the national statutes, and requested demotion to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gun could not contain his anger and memorialized that Youfu followed personal feeling to alter ritual, bent the national statutes, and requested demotion to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 德宗以為重，改河南少尹。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong considered it severe and changed the assignment to Vice Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong considered the penalty too harsh and changed the assignment to Vice Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 始肅宗時，天下務劇，宰相更直掌事，若休沐還第，非大詔命，不待遍曉，則聽直者代署以聞。

translations.literal: From the time of Emperor Suzong, affairs throughout the realm were pressing; chief ministers took turns on duty to handle business—if on rest days they returned home, unless it was a major edict or command, without waiting until all were informed, the one on duty might substitute signatures and report.
translations.idiomatic: From the time of Emperor Suzong, affairs throughout the realm were pressing; chief ministers took turns on duty—if on rest days they returned home, unless it was a major edict or command, without waiting until all were informed, the minister on duty might substitute signatures and report.

sentences.zh: 是時郭子儀、朱泚俱以平章事當署敕尾，而不行宰相事。

translations.literal: At that time Guo Ziyi and Zhu Ci, both holding the title of Grand Councilor, were to sign the tail of edicts, yet did not perform the duties of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Guo Ziyi and Zhu Ci, though both Grand Councilors, were only to sign the end of edicts and did not actually conduct the business of chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝新即位，袞如故事代署。

translations.literal: The emperor had newly ascended the throne; Gun, following precedent, substituted his signature.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had just taken the throne; Chang Gun, following established practice, signed in their stead.

sentences.zh: 子儀、泚入，言祐甫不宜貶，帝曰：「卿向何所言？

translations.literal: Ziyi and Ci entered and said Youfu ought not be demoted. The emperor said: "What did you two say before?
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi and Zhu Ci came in and argued that Youfu should not be demoted. The emperor said, "What did you tell me earlier?

sentences.zh: 今雲非邪？」

translations.literal: Now you say it is not so?"
translations.idiomatic: And now you say that was wrong?"

sentences.zh: 二人對初不知。

translations.literal: The two replied that at first they had not known.
translations.idiomatic: The two answered that they had not known at the time.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，以袞為罔上。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and judged Gun guilty of deceiving his superiors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and charged Gun with deceiving the throne.

sentences.zh: 是日，群臣苴绖立月華門外，即兩換職，以袞河南少尹，而拜祐甫門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: That day the officials, in hemp mourning garb, stood outside the Yuehua Gate; then both men were switched in office—Gun was made Vice Intendant of Henan, and Youfu was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: That day the officials stood outside the Yuehua Gate in hemp mourning dress; the two men were immediately exchanged in office—Gun was sent to be Vice Intendant of Henan, while Youfu was appointed Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 俄改中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自至德、乾元以來，天下戰討，啟丐填委，故官賞繆紊。

translations.literal: From the Zhide and Qianyuan eras onward the realm had been at war; memorials and pleas piled up in profusion, so appointments and rewards were confused and disorderly.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhide and Qianyuan eras onward the empire had been torn by war; petitions and requests flooded in, and appointments and rewards fell into chaos.

sentences.zh: 永泰後，稍稍平定，而元載用事，非賄謝不與官，刬塞公路，綱紀大壞。

translations.literal: After the Yongtai era things gradually settled, but Yuan Zai held power—without bribes and gifts he granted no office; he blocked the public road to advancement, and government discipline was greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongtai era the realm gradually quieted, but Yuan Zai held sway: no bribe, no appointment. He choked off the open path to office, and public order collapsed.

sentences.zh: 載誅，楊綰相，未幾卒。

translations.literal: When Zai was executed, Yang Wan became chancellor but died before long.
translations.idiomatic: Zai was put to death; Yang Wan became chief minister but died soon after.

sentences.zh: 袞當國，懲其敝，凡奏請一杜絕之，惟文辭入第乃得進，然無所甄異，賢愚同滯焉。

translations.literal: When Gun held national power, remedying these abuses, he cut off all such petitions entirely; only those whose literary compositions passed examination could advance—yet there was no differentiation, and worthy and foolish alike were stalled together.
translations.idiomatic: When Gun took charge of the state, he tried to cure these ills by shutting down every such request; only candidates whose literary compositions passed the examination could advance—yet he made no distinction among them, and the worthy and the worthless languished alike.

sentences.zh: 及祐甫，則薦舉惟其人，不自疑畏，推至公以行，未逾年，除吏幾八百員，莫不諧允。

translations.literal: When Youfu came, he recommended only the proper men, without self-doubt or fear, and proceeded with utmost fairness; within less than a year he appointed nearly eight hundred officials, and none failed to win approval.
translations.idiomatic: Under Youfu, recommendations went only to the right men; he acted without hesitation or fear, pushing fairness to its limit. In less than a year he appointed nearly eight hundred officials, and every choice met with general approval.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂曰：「人言卿擬官多親舊，何邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to him: "People say that in your nominations many are relatives and old friends—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked him, "People say you nominate mostly kin and old friends. Why is that?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「陛下令臣進擬庶官，夫進擬者必悉其才行，如不與聞知，何由得其實？」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your Majesty ordered me to submit nominations for ordinary officials. To nominate one must fully know his talent and conduct—if I am not personally acquainted, how could I obtain the truth?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Your Majesty commanded me to propose candidates for ordinary posts. To propose someone I must know his talent and character thoroughly—if I have no personal knowledge of him, how can I learn the truth?"

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the point.

sentences.zh: 神策軍使王駕鶴者，典衛兵久，權震中外，帝將代之，懼其變，以問祐甫，祐甫曰：「是無足慮。」

translations.literal: Wang Jiahe, commissioner of the Shence Army, had long commanded the imperial guards; his power shook court and countryside. When the emperor was about to replace him, fearing a revolt he asked Youfu. Youfu said: "That is not worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jiahe, commissioner of the Shence Army, had long held command of the palace guards, and his power awed both court and countryside. When the emperor planned to replace him, fearing trouble he consulted Youfu, who said, "There is nothing to worry about."

sentences.zh: 即召駕鶴留語移時，而代者已入軍中矣。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Jiahe and kept him in conversation for a long while, while the replacement had already entered the army.
translations.idiomatic: He at once summoned Jiahe and detained him in long conversation, while the new appointee was already inside the army camp.

sentences.zh: 淄青李正己畏帝威斷，表獻錢三十萬緡，以觀朝廷。

translations.literal: Li Zhengji of Ziqing, awed by the emperor's resolute authority, memorialized offering three hundred thousand strings of cash to test the court.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhengji of Ziqing, intimidated by the emperor's firm resolve, submitted a memorial offering three hundred thousand strings of cash to probe the court's response.

sentences.zh: 帝意其詐，未能答。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected deception but could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected a trick but did not know how to answer.

sentences.zh: 祐甫曰：「正己誠詐，陛下不如因遣使勞其軍，以所獻就賜將士。

translations.literal: Youfu said: "Zhengji is indeed being deceptive. Your Majesty would do better to take the opportunity to send an envoy to console his army and bestow the offered funds directly upon the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Youfu said, "Zhengji is indeed testing you. Your Majesty should seize the moment to send an envoy to comfort his troops and distribute the money he offered directly to the officers and men.

sentences.zh: 若正己奉承詔書，是陛下恩洽士心；

translations.literal: If Zhengji accepts and carries out the edict, then Your Majesty's grace will reach the hearts of the troops;
translations.idiomatic: If Zhengji accepts the edict and complies, Your Majesty's kindness will win the soldiers' hearts;

sentences.zh: 若不用，彼自斂怨，軍且亂。

translations.literal: if he does not use it, they will themselves gather resentment, and the army will soon be in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: if he refuses, his men will turn resentful on their own, and the army will soon fall into disorder.

sentences.zh: 又使諸藩不以朝廷為重賄。」

translations.literal: This also keeps the various garrison commands from treating the court as something to be bought with heavy bribes."
translations.idiomatic: It will also teach the other frontier commands not to treat the court as a prize to be bought with lavish bribes."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Good."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Excellent."

sentences.zh: 正己慚服。

translations.literal: Zhengji was ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengji, shamed, submitted.

sentences.zh: 時議者韙其謨謀，謂可復貞觀、開元之治。

translations.literal: Observers at the time praised his stratagems, saying the order of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras could be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries applauded his counsel and said the governance of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras might be restored.

sentences.zh: 是歲被疾，詔肩輿至中書，臥而承旨，若還第，即遣使咨決。

translations.literal: That year he fell ill; an edict ordered him carried by sedan to the Secretariat, where he lay and received imperial commands; when he returned home, envoys were sent to consult and decide affairs.
translations.idiomatic: That year he took ill. An edict ordered him brought by sedan chair to the Secretariat, where he lay abed and received the emperor's instructions; whenever he returned home, messengers were sent to consult him on decisions.

sentences.zh: 薨，年六十，贈太傅，謚曰文貞。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty; posthumously awarded Grand Mentor; posthumous title Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty. He was posthumously made Grand Mentor and given the posthumous name Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 故事，門下侍郎未有贈三師者，帝以其有大臣節，特寵異之。

translations.literal: By precedent no Vice Director of the Chancellery had ever been posthumously awarded one of the Three Preceptors; the emperor, because he possessed the integrity of a great minister, specially honored him.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent no Vice Director of the Chancellery had ever received posthumous appointment to one of the Three Preceptors; the emperor, holding that he had shown the mettle of a great minister, made an exception in his favor.

sentences.zh: 朱泚亂，祐甫妻王陷賊中，泚嘗與祐甫同列，遺以繒帛菽粟，受而緘鐍之，帝還京，具封以獻，士君子益重其家法雲。

translations.literal: During Zhu Ci's revolt, Youfu's wife Lady Wang was trapped among the rebels. Ci had once served alongside Youfu and sent her silk and grain; she accepted them but sealed and locked them away. When the emperor returned to the capital, she restored the sealed packages and presented them—all scholars and gentlemen esteemed her family discipline the more.
translations.idiomatic: During Zhu Ci's rebellion, Youfu's wife, Lady Wang, was caught behind rebel lines. Ci had once served with Youfu and sent her silk and grain; she accepted the gifts but sealed them untouched. When the emperor returned to the capital, she presented the packages intact, still sealed—and men of honor admired her household's rectitude all the more.

sentences.zh: 子植嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhi succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi carried on the line.

sentences.zh: 植字公修，祐甫弟廬江令嬰甫子也。

translations.literal: Zhi, courtesy name Gongxiu, was the son of Youfu's younger brother Yingfu, magistrate of Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi, styled Gongxiu, was the son of Youfu's younger brother Yingfu, magistrate of Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 祐甫病，謂妻曰：「吾歿，當以廬江次子主吾祀。」

translations.literal: When Youfu was ill he told his wife: "When I die, the second son in Lujiang should preside over my sacrifice."
translations.idiomatic: When Youfu fell ill he told his wife, "When I am gone, let the second son in Lujiang head my ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 及卒，護喪者以聞，帝惻然，召植，使即喪次終服。

translations.literal: When he died, those overseeing the mourning reported it; the emperor was moved, summoned Zhi, and had him immediately enter the mourning station and complete the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, those managing the funeral reported the matter. The emperor was deeply moved, summoned Zhi, and had him go straight to the mourning hall to complete the full period of filial observance.

sentences.zh: 補弘文生。

translations.literal: He was selected as a Hongwen Academy student.
translations.idiomatic: He was enrolled as a student of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 博通經史，於《易》尤邃。

translations.literal: Broadly versed in the classics and histories, he was especially deep in the Book of Changes.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the classics and histories and was especially profound in the Book of Changes.

sentences.zh: 與鄭覃同時為補闕，皆賢宰相後，每朝廷有得失，兩人者更疏論執，譽望蔚然。

translations.literal: Together with Zheng Tan he served as Reminder at the same time—both were sons of worthy chancellors; whenever the court had gains or faults, the two alternated in memorials stating their views, and their reputation rose like lush growth.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zheng Tan served together as Reminders—both sons of distinguished chief ministers. Whenever the court erred or excelled, the two took turns submitting memorials setting out their views, and their reputations flourished.

sentences.zh: 元和中，為給事中。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he served as Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe reign he became Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫镈判度支，建言減百官奉稟，植封還詔書。

translations.literal: At the time Huangfu Bo oversaw the Directorate of Public Works and proposed reducing all officials' salaries; Zhi returned the edict sealed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Huangfu Bo was in charge of fiscal affairs and proposed cutting the salaries of all officials. Zhi sealed and returned the edict.

sentences.zh: 镈又請天下所納鹽酒利增估者，以新準舊，一切追償。

translations.literal: Bo also requested that throughout the realm, where increased valuations on salt and wine profits had been paid, the new standard be applied retroactively to the old and all arrears be collected.
translations.idiomatic: Bo also asked that everywhere salt and wine profits had been paid at inflated valuations, the new rates be applied retroactively and the difference recovered in full.

sentences.zh: 植奏言：「用兵久，百姓雕罄，往雖估逾其實，今不可復收。」

translations.literal: Zhi memorialized: "War has lasted long and the people are exhausted; though past valuations exceeded the true value, they must not now be collected again."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi submitted a memorial: "The war has dragged on and the people are drained. Even if past assessments exceeded the true value, those sums cannot be collected again."

sentences.zh: 於是議者咸罪镈，镈懼而止。

translations.literal: Thereupon critics all blamed Bo, and Bo, frightened, stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The critics then all condemned Bo, and Bo, alarmed, abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Changqing era he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Changqing era he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗問：「貞觀、開元中治道最盛，何致而然？」

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong asked: "The governance of the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan eras was at its height—what brought that about?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong asked, "Under the Zhenguan and Kaiyuan reigns governance reached its peak—what made that so?"

sentences.zh: 植曰：「太宗資上聖，興民間，知百姓疾苦，故厲精思治，又以房玄齡、杜如晦、魏徵、王珪為之佐，君明臣忠，聖賢相維，治致升平，固其宜也。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "Taizong was endowed with supreme sagacity, rose from among the people, and knew the people's hardship; therefore he exerted himself in governing. Further, with Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Wei Zheng, and Wang Gui as his assistants—ruler enlightened, ministers loyal, sages and worthies supporting one another—order rising to peace was naturally fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Taizong possessed the highest wisdom, came up from among the people, and understood the people's suffering; so he applied himself tirelessly to governance. He had Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui, Wei Zheng, and Wang Gui as his aides—ruler clear-sighted, ministers loyal, sage and worthy men supporting one another—so peace and order were only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在天後時，身踐憂患，既即位，得姚崇、宋璟，此二人蚤夜孜孜，納君於道。

translations.literal: Xuanzong, during Empress Wu's reign, personally endured hardships; once enthroned he obtained Yao Chong and Song Jing—these two men morning and night tirelessly guided the ruler onto the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong, in Empress Wu's time, had himself lived through hardship; once enthroned he gained Yao Chong and Song Jing, who toiled day and night to keep the ruler on the right path.

sentences.zh: 珪嘗手寫《尚書》《無逸》，為圖以獻，勸帝出入觀省以自戒。

translations.literal: Gui once copied by hand the "Against Dissolute Leisure" chapter of the Book of Documents and made it into a pictorial scroll to present, urging the emperor whenever he went in or out to look upon it for self-warning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui once copied by hand the "Against Dissolute Leisure" from the Book of Documents and had it made into a hanging scroll, urging the emperor to read it whenever he passed in or out as a warning to himself.

sentences.zh: 其後朽暗，乃代以山水圖，稍怠於勤，左右不復箴規，奸臣日用事，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Later it rotted and darkened, and was replaced with a landscape painting; he slackened somewhat in diligence, those around him no longer admonished, scheming ministers daily held power, until ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: In time the scroll rotted and faded, and a landscape painting took its place. The emperor grew lax; those around him ceased to remonstrate; corrupt ministers gained ground day by day—and ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 昔德宗嘗問先臣祐甫開元、天寶事，先臣具道治亂所以然，臣在童鹴，記其說。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Dezong once asked my late father Youfu about Kaiyuan and Tianbao affairs; my late father fully explained why order and disorder arose thus. I was in childhood and remember his account.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong once asked my late father Youfu about the Kaiyuan and Tianbao periods, and my late father explained in full how order and chaos came about. I was still a boy then, but I remember what he said.

sentences.zh: 今願陛下以《無逸》為元龜，則天下幸甚。」

translations.literal: Now I wish Your Majesty would take "Against Dissolute Leisure" as a great mirror—then the realm would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will take "Against Dissolute Leisure" as your great mirror—the realm would be blessed indeed."

sentences.zh: 他日又問：「司馬遷言漢文帝惜十家產而罷露臺，身衣弋綈，履革舄，集上書囊為殿帷，信乎？

translations.literal: Another day he again asked: "Sima Qian says Emperor Wen of Han, to spare ten households' wealth, abandoned the Terrace of Dew; wore coarse silk, leather shoes, gathered satchels of memorials for hall curtains—is this true?
translations.idiomatic: On another day the emperor asked again, "Sima Qian says that Emperor Wen of Han, to spare the livelihood of ten households, canceled the Terrace of Dew; that he wore coarse silk, leather shoes, and made hall curtains from bundles of memorial satchels—is that true?

sentences.zh: 何太儉邪？」

translations.literal: How can he be so excessively frugal?"
translations.idiomatic: Was he not far too austere?"

sentences.zh: 植曰：「良史非兒言。

translations.literal: Zhi said: "A good historian does not speak like a child.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "A fine historian does not write childish tales.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦侈縱之餘，海內雕窶，文帝從代來，知稼穡艱難，是以躬履儉約，為天下守財。

translations.literal: Han inherited the excess and indulgence left by Qin; within the seas the people were impoverished. Emperor Wen came from Dai and knew the hardship of farming; therefore he personally practiced frugality and guarded wealth for the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Han rose on the ruins of Qin's extravagance; the land was destitute. Emperor Wen came from Dai and knew how hard farming was, so he lived plainly himself and hoarded wealth for the empire.

sentences.zh: 景帝遵而不改，故家給戶足。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing followed without change, hence each household had enough.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing kept to the same course, and households grew prosperous.

sentences.zh: 至武帝時，錢朽貫，谷紅腐，乃能出師征伐，威動四方；

translations.literal: By Emperor Wu's time strings of cash rotted, grain turned red and rotted—only then could he send armies on campaign and awe the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wu's day strings of cash rotted unused and grain soured in the granaries—only then could he march armies abroad and shake the four quarters.

sentences.zh: 然侈靡不節，末年戶口減半，稅及舟車，人不聊，乃下哀痛詔，封丞相為富人侯。

translations.literal: yet extravagance without restraint—in his late years the household register was halved, taxes reached boats and carts, people could not sustain life—then he issued the mournful edict and enfeoffed the chancellor as Marquis Rich Man.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he spent without limit. In his last years the population was halved, taxes fell even on boats and carts, and people could barely live. He then issued his lamentation edict and enfeoffed his chancellor as Marquis Rich Man.

sentences.zh: 然則帝王不可以不示儉而天下足。」

translations.literal: Thus an emperor cannot but display frugality and still have a realm abundantly provided."
translations.idiomatic: So it is that an emperor must show frugality if the realm is to prosper."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿言善，患行之為難耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What you say is good—the trouble is putting it into practice!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Well said—but the hard part is doing it!"

sentences.zh: 時朝廷悉收河朔三鎮，而劉總又以幽、薊七州獻諸朝，且懼部將構亂，乃先籍豪銳不檢者送京師，而朱克融在籍中。

translations.literal: At the time the court had fully recovered the three Hebei garrison commands, and Liu Zong also ceded seven prefectures of You and Ji to the court; fearing his subordinates would foment rebellion, he first registered unruly elite troops and sent them to the capital—and Zhu Kerong was on the register.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court had brought the three Hebei garrisons back under its control, and Liu Zong had also surrendered seven prefectures of You and Ji. Fearing mutiny among his officers, he first listed unruly elite troops and sent them to the capital—Zhu Kerong was among them.

sentences.zh: 植與杜元穎不知兵，謂蕃鎮且平，不復料天下安危事，而克融等羈旅塞躓，願得官自效，日訴於前，皆抑不與。

translations.literal: Zhi and Du Yuanying knew nothing of military affairs; they thought the frontier garrisons would soon be pacified and no longer weighed the realm's safety—while Kerong and others, stranded wanderers in dire straits, wished to win office by serving, daily pleading before them, all were suppressed and given nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi and Du Yuanying understood nothing of war. They assumed the frontier would soon be settled and stopped weighing the empire's safety. Kerong and his men, stranded far from home and desperate, begged daily for posts in which to prove themselves—but Zhi and Du turned them all away.

sentences.zh: 及遣張弘靖赴鎮，縱克融等北還，不數月，克融亂，復失河朔矣。

translations.literal: When Zhang Hongjing was sent to take up the garrison command and Kerong and others were released to return north, within a few months Kerong rebelled and the Hebei region was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Hongjing was dispatched to take command and Kerong and the others were allowed to go north, within months Kerong rose in rebellion and Hebei was lost again.

sentences.zh: 天下尤之，植內慚。

translations.literal: The realm blamed them; Zhi was inwardly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The empire held them responsible; Zhi was consumed with shame.

sentences.zh: 罷為刑部尚書，旋授嶽鄂觀察使。

translations.literal: Dismissed from the chancellorship and made Minister of Justice; soon appointed Regional Inspector of Yue and E.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of the chancellorship, he was made Minister of Justice, then soon sent out as Regional Inspector of Yue and E.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷嶺南節度使，還拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long transferred to military commissioner of Lingnan; on return appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he was transferred to military commissioner of Lingnan; on returning to court he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 終華州刺史，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: Ended as prefect of Hua; posthumously awarded Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as prefect of Hua and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 倰，字德長，祐甫從子也。

translations.literal: Jun, courtesy name Dechang, was Youfu's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Dechang, was Youfu's nephew.

sentences.zh: 性介潔，矜己之清，視贓負者若讎。

translations.literal: By nature stern and fastidious, proud of his own purity, he treated the corrupt as if they were foes.
translations.idiomatic: He was rigid and scrupulous by nature, proud of his own integrity, and looked on the corrupt as enemies.

sentences.zh: 以蘇州刺史奏課第一，遷湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: As prefect of Suzhou his annual assessment ranked first; promoted to Regional Inspector of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Suzhou his annual evaluation ranked first, and he was promoted to Regional Inspector of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 湖南舊法，雖豐年，貿易不出境，鄰部災荒不恤也。

translations.literal: Hunan's old law held that even in plentiful years trade did not cross the border, and neighboring districts in famine received no aid.
translations.idiomatic: An old Hunan regulation barred trade from crossing the border even in good harvest years, leaving neighboring regions in famine to fend for themselves.

sentences.zh: 倰至，謂屬吏曰：「此豈人情乎？

translations.literal: When Jun arrived he said to subordinate officials: "Is this human feeling?
translations.idiomatic: When Jun took office he told his staff, "Is this any way to treat one's fellow men?

sentences.zh: 無閉糴以重困民。」

translations.literal: Do not close off grain trade to add weight to the people's distress."
translations.idiomatic: Do not shut down grain trade and deepen the people's hardship."

sentences.zh: 削其禁，自是商賈流通，貲物益饒。

translations.literal: He abolished the prohibition; from then on merchants circulated and goods grew abundant.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted the ban; from then on commerce flowed freely and goods grew plentiful.

sentences.zh: 入為戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: Entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue, with concurrent duty over fiscal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Vice Minister of Revenue with concurrent charge of fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 時田弘正徙鎮州，以魏兵二千行。

translations.literal: At the time Tian Hongzheng transferred to Zhenzhou, taking two thousand Wei troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tian Hongzheng was transferred to Zhenzhou, bringing two thousand Wei soldiers with him.

sentences.zh: 既至，留自衛，請度支給歲糧，穆宗下其議，倰固執不與，弘正不得已，遣魏卒。

translations.literal: When he arrived he kept them for self-defense and requested annual grain from the fiscal directorate; Emperor Muzong referred the matter for discussion—Jun stubbornly refused. Hongzheng had no choice and sent the Wei soldiers away.
translations.idiomatic: Once there he kept the troops for his own protection and asked the fiscal office for annual grain rations. Emperor Muzong referred the request for deliberation, but Jun stubbornly refused. Hongzheng had no choice but to dismiss the Wei soldiers.

sentences.zh: 俄而鎮兵亂，弘正遇害，倰之為也。

translations.literal: Soon the Zhenzhou troops mutinied and Hongzheng was killed—it was Jun's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Zhenzhou garrison mutinied and Hongzheng was killed—Jun had brought it about.

sentences.zh: 時天子失德，倰黨與盛，有司不敢名其罪。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven had lost virtue; Jun's faction was powerful, and the authorities dared not name his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had fallen into moral decline; Jun's clique was strong, and the officials dared not charge him openly.

sentences.zh: 出為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: Sent out as military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙河南尹。

translations.literal: After a year transferred to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書致仕，卒，贈太子少保，謚曰肅。

translations.literal: Retired as Minister of Revenue; died; posthumously awarded Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince; posthumous title Su.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Minister of Revenue and died. He was posthumously made Junior Mentor to the Crown Prince and given the posthumous name Su.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：植輔政，當有為之時，無經國才，履危防淺，機不知其潰而發也，手弛檻緤，縱虎狼焉，一日而亡地數千里，為天下笑；

translations.literal: Comment: Zhi assisted in government at a time when action was needed, yet lacked talent to order the state; treading danger with shallow defenses, he did not know the breach forming until it burst—he personally loosed bars and chains and released tiger and wolf; in a day territory of several thousand li was lost and the realm laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Comment: Zhi held power when the state needed bold action, yet he lacked the talent to govern a nation. He walked the edge of peril with feeble precautions, never seeing the dam burst until it broke—he himself loosened the cage and let the tiger and wolf loose; in a single day thousands of li of territory were lost, and the empire laughed.

sentences.zh: 倰吝財資賊。

translations.literal: Jun was stingy with treasury funds—a villain.
translations.idiomatic: Jun hoarded the public purse—a knave.

sentences.zh: 又皆幸不誅。

translations.literal: Yet both by fortune escaped execution.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both, by luck, escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 天以河北亂唐，故君臣不肖，勃繆其謀，惜哉！

translations.literal: Heaven used Hebei to disorder Tang, therefore ruler and ministers were unworthy and wildly tangled their schemes—alas!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven meant Hebei to undo Tang, and so ruler and ministers alike proved unworthy, tangling their plans in chaos—what a pity!

sentences.zh: 柳渾，字夷曠，一字惟深，本名載，梁僕射惔六世孫，後籍襄州。

translations.literal: Liu Hun, courtesy name Yikuang, also styled Weishen; original name Zai; sixth-generation descendant of Liang Vice Director Tan; later registered household in Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hun, styled Yikuang and also Weishen, originally named Zai, was a sixth-generation descendant of Tan, Vice Director under Liang; his family later registered in Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 早孤，方十餘歲，有巫告曰：「兒相夭且賤，為浮屠道可緩死。」

translations.literal: Orphaned early, barely over ten, a shaman said: "The boy's physiognomy shows early death and low station; entering the Buddhist path may defer death."
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father young. When he was barely past ten a shaman said, "This boy's face marks him for early death and low rank; take the Buddhist path and death may be delayed."

sentences.zh: 諸父欲從其言，渾曰：「去聖教，為異術，不若速死。」

translations.literal: His uncles wished to follow this advice; Hun said: "To leave the sage's teaching and follow heterodox arts—better to die quickly."
translations.idiomatic: His uncles wanted to heed this, but Hun said, "To abandon the sage's teaching for alien arts—I would rather die at once."

sentences.zh: 學愈篤，與遊者皆有名士。

translations.literal: He studied all the more diligently; those he befriended were all men of name.
translations.idiomatic: He applied himself to learning all the harder, and everyone he kept company with was a man of reputation.

sentences.zh: 天寶初，擢進士第，調單父尉，累除衢州司馬。

translations.literal: In the early Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, appointed magistrate of Shanfu, successively promoted to Vice Prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Tianbao era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Shanfu, and rose in time to Vice Prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 棄官隱武寧山。

translations.literal: He abandoned office and hid on Mount Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned his post and withdrew to Mount Wuning.

sentences.zh: 召拜監察御史，臺僚以儀矩相繩，而渾放曠不樂檢局，乃求外職。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Investigating Censor; the censorate staff bound one another with ritual standards, but Hun was free and unrestrained, disliking restraint—so he sought an outer post.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and made Investigating Censor. The censorate bound its members with strict protocol, but Hun was free-spirited and chafed at confinement, so he asked for an outside appointment.

sentences.zh: 宰相惜其才，留為左補闕。

translations.literal: The chief minister prized his talent and kept him as Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister valued his ability and retained him as Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 大歷初，江西魏少遊表為判官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dali era, Wei Shaoyou of Jiangxi recommended him as administrative aide.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Dali era, Wei Shaoyou of Jiangxi recommended him as administrative aide.

sentences.zh: 州僧有夜飲火其廬者，歸罪瘖奴，軍候受財不詰，獄具，渾與其僚崔祐甫白奴冤，少遊趣訊僧，僧首伏，因厚謝二人。

translations.literal: A monk in the prefecture, after drinking at night, set fire to his own dwelling and blamed a mute slave; the military inspector accepted bribes and did not investigate—the case was settled. Hun and his colleague Cui Youfu reported the slave's innocence; Shaoyou urgently questioned the monk, who confessed at the head, and richly thanked the two.
translations.idiomatic: A monk in the prefecture, drunk one night, burned his own quarters and blamed a mute slave. The military inspector took a bribe and closed the inquiry; the case was judged. Hun and his colleague Cui Youfu reported the slave's innocence. Shaoyou hurried to interrogate the monk, who confessed outright, and he richly rewarded the two men.

sentences.zh: 路嗣恭代少遊，渾遷團練副使。

translations.literal: Lu Sichong replaced Shaoyou; Hun was promoted to deputy commissioner of militia training.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Sichong replaced Shaoyou, Hun was promoted to deputy commissioner of militia training.

sentences.zh: 俄為袁州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he became prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祐甫輔政，薦為諫議大夫、浙江東西黜陟使。

translations.literal: When Youfu assisted in government, he recommended him as Remonstrance Grand Master and Investigating Commissioner for Zhejiang East and West.
translations.idiomatic: When Youfu took power, he recommended Hun as Remonstrance Grand Master and Investigating Commissioner for Zhejiang East and West.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 朱泚亂，渾匿終南山。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Hun hid on Mount Zhongnan.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rebelled, Liu Hun went into hiding on Mount Zhongnan.

sentences.zh: 賊素聞其名，以宰相召，執其子搒笞之，搜索所在。

translations.literal: The rebels had long heard his name; summoning him as chief minister, they seized his son and beat him with the cudgel, searching for where he was.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had long known his reputation. They summoned him to serve as chief minister, seized his son and flogged him, and searched everywhere for his hiding place.

sentences.zh: 渾羸服步至奉天，改右散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Hun, in emaciated shabby clothes, walked to Fengtian; was changed to Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Emaciated and in threadbare clothes, Hun walked to Fengtian, where he was appointed Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 賊平，奏言：「臣名向為賊汙，且『載』於文從戈，非偃武所宜。」

translations.literal: When the rebels were quelled, he memorialized: "Your servant's name has been befouled by the rebels, and moreover the character 'Zai' in its written form follows the radical for spear—unsuitable for a time to lay down arms."
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was suppressed, he submitted a memorial: "My name has been tainted by the rebels, and moreover the character for Zai, in its written form, carries the spear radical—hardly fitting for an era meant to sheathe the sword."

sentences.zh: 乃更今名。

translations.literal: He then changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He then took his present name.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，遷兵部侍郎，封宜城縣伯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, he was transferred to Vice Minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Yicheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhenyuan era, he was promoted to Vice Minister of War and enfeoffed as Baron of Yicheng County.

sentences.zh: 李希烈據淮、蔡，關播用李元平守汝州，渾曰：「是夫衒玉而賈石者也。

translations.literal: Li Xilie held Huai and Cai; Guan Bo appointed Li Yuanping to defend Ruzhou. Hun said: "That man is one who displays jade while selling stone.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xilie held Huai and Cai. Guan Bo put Li Yuanping in charge of defending Ruzhou. Hun said, "That man is the sort who shows jade but sells stone.

sentences.zh: 往必見禽，何賊之攘？」

translations.literal: If he goes he will surely be taken—how will the rebels be driven off?"
translations.idiomatic: Send him and he will surely be captured—how will that drive off the rebels?"

sentences.zh: 既而果為賊縛。

translations.literal: Before long he was indeed bound by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Yuanping was indeed seized by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 三年，以本官同中書門下平章事，仍判門下省。

translations.literal: In the third year, with his current rank he became Associate Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and concurrently oversaw the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made Associate Councilor of the Secretariat and Chancellery at his existing rank, and concurrently placed in charge of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗親擇吏宰畿邑，而政有狀，召宰相語，皆賀帝得人，渾獨不賀，曰：「此特京兆尹職耳。

translations.literal: The emperor once personally selected an official to govern a capital district; when his administration showed results, he summoned the chief ministers to speak—all congratulated the emperor on finding the right man, but Hun alone did not congratulate, saying: "This is merely the duty of the Jingzhao Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once personally chose an official to govern a district in the capital region. When that man's administration proved effective, he summoned the chief ministers to discuss it. All congratulated the emperor on finding the right man, but Hun alone withheld his praise, saying, "This is simply the Jingzhao Intendant's job.

sentences.zh: 陛下當擇臣輩以輔聖德，臣當選京兆尹承大化，尹當求令長親細事。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should select us ministers to assist your sagely virtue; we should select the Jingzhao Intendant to carry out the great transformation; the Intendant should seek district magistrates to handle detailed affairs in person.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should choose us ministers to assist your sagely virtue; we should choose the Jingzhao Intendant to carry out the great transformation; the Intendant should find district magistrates to handle detailed affairs in person.

sentences.zh: 代尹擇令，非陛下所宜。」

translations.literal: For you to replace the Intendant in selecting magistrates is not what Your Majesty should do."
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty to step in and choose magistrates in the Intendant's place is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 帝然之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 玉工為帝作帶，誤毀一銙，工不敢聞，私市它玉足之。

translations.literal: A jade craftsman making a belt for the emperor accidentally destroyed one link; the craftsman dared not report it and secretly bought other jade to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: A jade craftsman making a belt for the emperor accidentally broke one link. The craftsman dared not report it and secretly bought other jade to make up the loss.

sentences.zh: 及獻，帝識不類，擿之，工人伏罪。

translations.literal: When it was presented, the emperor recognized it was not the same and exposed it; the craftsman confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: When the belt was presented, the emperor recognized that the jade was not the same and exposed the fraud. The craftsman confessed his crime.

sentences.zh: 帝怒其欺，詔京兆府論死，渾曰：「陛下遽殺之則已，若委有司，須詳讞乃可。

translations.literal: The emperor, angry at the deception, ordered the Jingzhao office to sentence him to death. Hun said: "If Your Majesty kills him outright, so be it; but if you hand it to the officials, a detailed verdict is required first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, furious at the deception, ordered the Jingzhao office to sentence the craftsman to death. Hun said, "If Your Majesty executes him at once, so be it; but if the matter is entrusted to the officials, a full inquiry must be completed first.

sentences.zh: 於法，誤傷乘輿器服，罪當杖，請論如律。」

translations.literal: By law, accidentally damaging the emperor's carriage implements and apparel warrants beating with the rod. I request sentencing according to the statutes."
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, accidentally damaging the emperor's carriage fittings and regalia calls for beating with the rod. I ask that he be sentenced accordingly."

sentences.zh: 由是工不死。

translations.literal: Thus the craftsman was not executed.
translations.idiomatic: As a result the craftsman was not put to death.

sentences.zh: 左丞田季羔從子伯強請賣私第募兵助討吐蕃，渾曰：「季羔，先朝號名臣，由祖以來世孝謹，表闕於門，隋時舊第，惟田一族耳。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director Tian Jigao's nephew Baqiang requested to sell the family mansion to raise troops to help campaign against Tibet. Hun said: "Jigao was called a famous minister in the previous reign; from his grandfather's time the family has been filial and careful for generations, with plaques of honor at the gate—the old Sui mansion is the Tian clan's sole estate.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jigao, the Left Assistant Director, had a nephew named Baqiang who asked to sell the family residence to raise troops for the campaign against Tibet. Hun said, "Jigao was renowned as a distinguished minister in the previous reign. For generations, from his grandfather's time, the Tian family has been filial and scrupulous, with honor plaques at their gate. That old Sui-era mansion is the sole property of the entire Tian clan.

sentences.zh: 討賊自有國計，豈容不肖子毀門構，僥一時幸，損風教哉！

translations.literal: Campaigns against enemies have the state's own plans—how can an unworthy son be allowed to destroy the family's gate and structure, gambling on a moment's luck and damaging custom and teaching!
translations.idiomatic: Campaigns against the enemy are matters of state policy—how can an unworthy son be permitted to tear down the family gate and halls, gambling on a moment's favor and damaging public morals!

sentences.zh: 請薄責以示懲沮！」

translations.literal: I request light punishment to show deterrence!"
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he receive light punishment as a warning to others!"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 韓滉自浙西入朝，帝虛己待之，奏事或日晏，他相取充位，滉遂省中搒吏自若。

translations.literal: Han Huang entered court from Zhexi; the emperor treated him with humble deference; when memorializing affairs sometimes until dusk, the other chief ministers were merely placeholders, and Huang beat clerks in the Secretariat as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Han Huang came to court from Zhexi. The emperor received him with deferential humility. When Huang reported on affairs, sessions sometimes lasted until dusk, while the other chief ministers were little more than figureheads. Huang then beat clerks in the Secretariat at will.

sentences.zh: 渾雖為滉所引，惡其專，質讓曰：「省闥非刑人地，而搒吏至死。
