translations.literal: Though Hun had been promoted by Huang, he detested his arbitrary power and remonstrated face to face: "The Secretariat is no place for punishing people, yet you beat clerks to death.
translations.idiomatic: Though Hun owed his advancement to Huang, he detested Huang's autocratic ways and confronted him directly: "The Secretariat is no place for corporal punishment, yet you beat clerks to death.

sentences.zh: 公家先相國以狷察，不滿歲輒罷，今公柰何蹈前非，顓立威福？

translations.literal: Your family's former chief minister was dismissed within the year for being narrow and sharp-eyed—why do you now tread the same wrong path and monopolize authority and favor?
translations.idiomatic: Your family's former chief minister was removed within a year for being narrow and harsh in his scrutiny—why do you now repeat that mistake and monopolize power and favor?

sentences.zh: 豈尊主卑臣義邪？」

translations.literal: Is this the principle of honoring the ruler and keeping ministers low?"
translations.idiomatic: Is this what it means to honor the ruler and keep ministers in their proper place?"

sentences.zh: 滉悔悟，稍褫其威。

translations.literal: Huang repented and gradually curbed his power.
translations.idiomatic: Huang took the rebuke to heart and gradually moderated his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 白誌貞除浙西觀察使，渾奏：「誌貞興小史，縱嘉其才，不當超劇職。

translations.literal: Bai Zhizhen was appointed observation commissioner of Zhexi. Hun memorialized: "Zhizhen rose from a minor clerk; even if one praises his talent, he should not leap to a difficult post.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Zhizhen was appointed observation commissioner of Zhexi. Hun submitted a memorial: "Zhizhen rose from a minor clerk. Even if one admires his talent, he should not be jumped into so demanding a post.

sentences.zh: 臣以死守，不敢奉詔。」

translations.literal: Your servant will die holding firm—I dare not obey the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant would rather die than comply—I dare not obey this edict."

sentences.zh: 會渾移疾出，即日詔付外施行。

translations.literal: Just as Hun fell ill and left, that very day an edict ordered it carried out outside the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Hun took sick leave, an edict was issued that same day ordering the appointment implemented without further review.

sentences.zh: 疾間，因乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: When his illness eased, he requested retirement but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness abated, he asked to retire, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 門下吏白過官，渾愀然曰：「既委有司，而復橈之，豈賢者用心邪？

translations.literal: A Chancellery clerk reported a passing appointment; Hun said somberly: "Once matters are delegated to officials and then overridden—is this how the worthy use their minds?
translations.idiomatic: A Chancellery clerk reported a routine appointment for approval. Hun said grimly, "Once a matter is entrusted to the proper officials, only to have it overturned—is that how a worthy man should conduct himself?

sentences.zh: 士或千里辭家以幹祿，小邑主辦，豈慮不能？」

translations.literal: A gentleman may leave home for a thousand li seeking office—a district magistrate handling affairs—would he worry he cannot manage?"
translations.idiomatic: A gentleman may travel a thousand li from home seeking office—is a district magistrate, handling local affairs, really unable to manage?"

sentences.zh: 是歲擬官，無退異者。

translations.literal: That year, for proposed appointments, there were none rejected or altered.
translations.idiomatic: That year, not a single proposed appointment was rejected or changed.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊與吐蕃會平涼，是日，帝語大臣以和戎息師之便。

translations.literal: Hun Zhen met with Tibet at Pingliang. That day the emperor told the ministers of the advantages of appeasing the barbarians and resting the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Zhen met with the Tibetans at Pingliang. That same day the emperor told his ministers of the benefits of making peace with the barbarians and standing down the armies.

sentences.zh: 馬燧賀曰：「今日已盟，可百年無虜患。」

translations.literal: Ma Sui congratulated: "Today the alliance is made—we may be free of barbarian trouble for a hundred years."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sui offered congratulations: "The alliance is made today—we may be free of barbarian trouble for a hundred years."

sentences.zh: 渾跪曰：「五帝無誥誓，三王無盟詛，蓋盟詛之興皆在季末。

translations.literal: Hun knelt and said: "The Five Emperors had no proclamations and oaths; the Three Kings had no covenants and curses—for covenants and curses arise only at the end of ages.
translations.idiomatic: Hun knelt and said, "The Five Emperors knew no proclamations and oaths; the Three Kings knew no covenants and curses. Such oaths arise only at the end of an age.

sentences.zh: 今盛明之朝，反以季末事行於夷狄。

translations.literal: Now in this flourishing enlightened court, we reverse and apply end-of-age practices toward barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in this flourishing and enlightened age, we resort to practices of a decadent era in dealing with barbarians.

sentences.zh: 夫夷狄人面獸心，易以兵制，難以信結，臣竊憂之。」

translations.literal: Barbarians have human faces but beast hearts—they are easily controlled by arms, hard to bind by trust. Your servant secretly worries."
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians have the faces of men but the hearts of beasts. They are easily controlled by force and hard to bind with trust. I am deeply troubled by this."

sentences.zh: 李晟繼言曰：「蕃戎多不情，誠如渾言。」

translations.literal: Li Sheng added: "The Fan barbarians are mostly faithless—truly as Hun says."
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng added, "The Fan barbarians are mostly faithless—exactly as Hun says."

sentences.zh: 帝變色曰：「渾，儒生，未達邊事，而大臣亦當爾邪？」

translations.literal: The emperor changed countenance and said: "Hun, a Confucian scholar, does not understand border affairs—and should senior ministers speak thus as well?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression darkened. "Hun is a Confucian scholar who does not understand frontier affairs—and should senior ministers speak this way as well?"

sentences.zh: 皆頓首謝。

translations.literal: All knocked their heads and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: All prostrated themselves and apologized.

sentences.zh: 夜半，邠寧節度使韓遊瑰飛奏吐蕃劫盟，將校皆覆沒。

translations.literal: At midnight, Binning Military Commissioner Han Yougui's urgent memorial reported Tibet had violated the alliance; officers and commanders were all lost.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight an urgent dispatch arrived from Han Yougui, military commissioner of Binning, reporting that the Tibetans had broken the alliance and that officers and commanders had been wiped out.

sentences.zh: 帝大驚，即以其表示渾。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly alarmed and immediately showed the memorial to Hun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly alarmed and immediately showed the dispatch to Hun.

sentences.zh: 明日，慰之曰：「卿，儒士，乃知軍戎萬里情乎？」

translations.literal: The next day he comforted him: "You, a Confucian scholar—yet you knew the situation a thousand li away on the frontier?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he comforted him, saying, "You are a Confucian scholar—yet you knew what was happening a thousand li away on the frontier?"

sentences.zh: 益禮異之。

translations.literal: He honored him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the emperor treated him with special regard.

sentences.zh: 宰相張延賞怙權，嫉渾守正，遣親厚謂曰：「明公舊德，弟慎言於朝，則位可久。」

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Yanshang relied on power, resented Hun's uprightness, and sent a close associate to say: "Your old merit, sir—if you are cautious in speech at court, your position may last long."
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Yanshang, relying on his power, resented Hun's rectitude and sent a close associate to tell him, "With your long-standing merit, sir, if you are careful in what you say at court, your position may endure."

sentences.zh: 渾曰：「為吾謝張公，渾頭可斷，而舌不可禁。」

translations.literal: Hun said: "Give my thanks to Lord Zhang—Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced."
translations.idiomatic: Hun replied, "Give my thanks to Lord Zhang. Hun's head may be cut off, but his tongue cannot be silenced."

sentences.zh: 卒為所擠，以右散騎常侍罷政事。

translations.literal: In the end he was forced out, dismissed from government affairs as Right Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was driven out and removed from office, retaining only the title of Right Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 渾警辯好談謔，與人交，豁如也。

translations.literal: Hun was alert in debate and fond of jest; in dealing with people he was open and free.
translations.idiomatic: Hun was quick-witted and fond of banter. In his dealings with others he was open and unreserved.

sentences.zh: 情儉不營產利。

translations.literal: By nature frugal, he did not pursue profit in property.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was frugal and did not seek profit in property.

sentences.zh: 免後數日，置酒召故人出遊，酣肆乃還，曠然無黜免意。

translations.literal: A few days after dismissal he set out wine, summoned old friends to go roaming; drunk and unrestrained he returned, utterly without the air of one demoted.
translations.idiomatic: A few days after his dismissal he set out wine, invited old friends on an outing, and returned drunk and carefree, showing not the slightest trace of one who had been removed from office.

sentences.zh: 時李勉、盧翰皆以舊相闔門奉朝請，嘆曰：「吾等視柳宜城，真拘俗之人哉！」

translations.literal: At the time Li Mian and Lu Han, both former chief ministers, brought their whole households as court attendees; they sighed: "Compared with us, is Lord Liu of Yicheng truly a man bound by vulgar convention?"
translations.idiomatic: At the time Li Mian and Lu Han, both former chief ministers, brought their entire households to attend court as idle retainers. They sighed, "When we look at Lord Liu of Yicheng, are we not the ones truly bound by vulgar convention?"

sentences.zh: 五年卒，年七十五，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died, aged seventy-five; posthumous name Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died at seventy-five. His posthumous name was Zhen, Upright.

sentences.zh: 渾母兄識，字方明，知名士也。

translations.literal: Hun's maternal elder cousin Shi, courtesy name Fangming, was a man of renown.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's maternal elder cousin Shi, styled Fangming, was a man of established reputation.

sentences.zh: 工文章，與蕭穎士、元德秀、劉迅相上下，而識練理創端，往往詣極，雖趣尚非博，然當時作者伏其簡拔。

translations.literal: Skilled in literary composition, he was on par with Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun; but Shi mastered principle and opened themes, often reaching the utmost—though his interests were not broad, writers of the age respected his terse elevation.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in literary composition and ranked with Xiao Yingshi, Yuan Dexiu, and Liu Xun. Yet Shi mastered principle and opened new themes, often reaching their utmost expression. Though his interests were not wide-ranging, writers of the age respected his terse brilliance.

sentences.zh: 渾亦善屬文，但沈思不逮於識雲。

translations.literal: Hun also composed well, but in deep reflection he did not reach Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Hun could also write well, but in depth of thought he did not match Shi.

sentences.zh: 韋處厚，字德載，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Chuhou, courtesy name Dezai, was a man of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chuhou, styled Dezai, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 事繼母以孝聞，親歿，廬墓終喪。

translations.literal: He was famed for filial service to his stepmother; when his parents died he kept a mourning hut at the tomb through the full mourning period.
translations.idiomatic: He was known for filial devotion to his stepmother. When his parents died, he kept a mourning hut at their tomb through the full mourning period.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，又擢才識兼茂科，授集賢校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was also selected in the Magnificent Talent and Comprehensive Knowledge special examination, appointed collator in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was also selected in the Magnificent Talent and Comprehensive Knowledge special examination, then appointed collator in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正異等，宰相裴垍引直史館。

translations.literal: Recommended as Exceptionally Excellent in the Filial and Incorrupt examination, Chief Minister Pei Ji brought him into the History Institute as direct compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as Exceptionally Excellent in the Filial and Incorrupt examination, he was brought into the History Institute as a direct compiler by Chief Minister Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 改咸陽尉。

translations.literal: Changed to magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初，擢左補闕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzong's reign, promoted to Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xianzong's reign he was promoted to Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 禮部尚書李絳請間言：「古帝王以納諫為聖，拒諫為昏。

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies Li Jiang requested a private audience and said: "Ancient emperors took accepting remonstrance as sagely and rejecting remonstrance as benighted.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Ceremonies Li Jiang asked for a private audience and said, "Ancient emperors were deemed sage when they accepted remonstrance and benighted when they rejected it.

sentences.zh: 今不聞進規納忠，何以知天下事？」

translations.literal: Now we hear no one offering counsel and loyally serving—how are we to know affairs under heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Today we hear no one offering counsel and serving loyally—how then can we know what is happening under heaven?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「韋處厚、路隋數上疏，其言忠切，顧卿未知爾。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Wei Chuhou and Lu Sui have repeatedly submitted memorials—their words are loyal and earnest—but you perhaps did not know this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wei Chuhou and Lu Sui have submitted memorials repeatedly. Their words are loyal and earnest—you simply did not know of them."

sentences.zh: 由是中外推其靖密。

translations.literal: From this inside and outside the court esteemed his quiet discretion.
translations.idiomatic: From this, inside and outside the court, people respected his quiet discretion.

sentences.zh: 歷考功員外郎，坐與宰相韋貫之善，出開州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel; punished for friendship with Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi, he was sent out as prefect of Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Assistant Director in the Ministry of Personnel. Because of his friendship with Chief Minister Wei Guanzhi, he was sent out as prefect of Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 以戶部郎中入知制誥。

translations.literal: Entering as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue, he took charge of drafting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue and took charge of drafting edicts.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，為翰林侍講學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended, he became Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong came to the throne, he was made Hanlin Attendant Lecturer.

sentences.zh: 處厚以帝沖怠不向學，即與路隋合《易》、《書》、《詩》、《春秋》、《禮》、《孝經》、《論語》，掇其粹要，題為《六經法言》二十篇上之，冀助省覽。

translations.literal: Chuhou, because the emperor was young, slack, and disinclined to study, together with Lu Sui compiled essentials from the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, Rites, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects, titled "Selected Explications of the Six Classics" in twenty chapters and presented them, hoping to aid his reading.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor was young, idle, and disinclined to study, Chuhou joined with Lu Sui to extract the essential teachings from the Changes, Documents, Odes, Spring and Autumn, Rites, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects. They compiled these into twenty chapters titled Selected Explications of the Six Classics and presented them to the throne, hoping to aid his reading.

sentences.zh: 帝稱善，並賜金幣。

translations.literal: The emperor praised them and granted gold and silk to both.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the work and granted gold and silk to both men.

sentences.zh: 再遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Secretariat Drafting Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Secretariat Drafting Officer.

sentences.zh: 張平叔以言利得幸於帝，建言官自鬻鹽，籠天下之財。

translations.literal: Zhang Pingshu, through talk of profit winning the emperor's favor, proposed government monopoly salt sales to gather the realm's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Pingshu won the emperor's favor through talk of profit and proposed that the government monopolize the sale of salt to gather the wealth of the realm.

sentences.zh: 宰相不能詰，下群臣議，處厚發十難誚其迂謬，平叔愧縮，遂寢。

translations.literal: The chief ministers could not refute him; the matter was sent down for discussion among ministers. Chuhou raised ten difficulties mocking the proposal as absurd; Pingshu shrank in shame, and the plan was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers could not refute him, so the proposal was sent down for discussion among the ministers. Chuhou raised ten objections exposing its absurdity. Pingshu shrank in shame, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 敬宗初，李逢吉得柄，構李紳，逐為端州司馬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Jingzong's reign, Li Fengji gained power, framed Li Shen, and banished him as Vice Prefect of Duanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Jingzong's reign, Li Fengji seized power, framed Li Shen, and banished him as vice prefect of Duanzhou.

sentences.zh: 其黨劉棲楚等欲致紳必死，建言當徙醜地。

translations.literal: His faction Liu Qichu and others sought to ensure Shen's death, proposing he be transferred to a desolate place.
translations.idiomatic: His faction, including Liu Qichu, sought to ensure Shen's death and proposed transferring him to a harsher region.

sentences.zh: 處厚上言：「逢吉黨與，以紳之斥猶有餘辜，人情危駭。

translations.literal: Chuhou submitted: "Fengji's clique, treating Shen's banishment as still leaving guilt unpunished—people's minds are alarmed and frightened.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou submitted a memorial: "Fengji's faction treats Shen's banishment as if his guilt were still not fully punished. The people are alarmed and frightened.

sentences.zh: 《詩》云『萋兮斐兮，成是貝錦。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'How lush, how luxuriant—thus is brocade fashioned.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say, 'How lush, how luxuriant—thus is brocade fashioned.

sentences.zh: 彼譖人者，亦已太甚』，『讒言罔極，交亂四國』。

translations.literal: Those who slander others—they go too far,' 'Slander knows no limit, throwing the four states into turmoil.'
translations.idiomatic: Those who slander others have gone too far,' and, 'Slander knows no limit, throwing the four states into turmoil.'

sentences.zh: 此古人疾讒之深也。

translations.literal: This shows how deeply the ancients hated slander.
translations.idiomatic: This shows how deeply the ancients hated slander.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『三年無改於父之道，可謂孝矣。』

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Three years without altering his father's way may be called filial.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Three years without altering his father's way may be called filial.

sentences.zh: 按紳先朝舊臣，就令有過，尚當祓瑕洗釁，成無改之美，況被讒乎！

translations.literal: Shen is an old minister of the previous reign—even if he had faults, one should still cleanse blemishes and wash away guilt to complete the beauty of unchanging loyalty—how much more when he was slandered!
translations.idiomatic: Shen is an old minister of the previous reign. Even if he had faults, one should still cleanse his blemishes and wash away his guilt to preserve the beauty of unchanging loyalty—how much more so when he has been slandered!

sentences.zh: 建中時，山東之亂興，宰相朋黨，楊炎為元載復讎，盧杞為劉晏償怨，兵連禍結，天下騷然。

translations.literal: In the Jianzhong era the Shandong rebellions arose; chief ministers formed factions—Yang Yan avenged Yuan Zai, Lu Qi repaid a grudge against Liu Yan—war linked with disaster, the realm in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianzhong era rebellions broke out in Shandong. Chief ministers formed factions: Yang Yan avenged Yuan Zai, Lu Qi settled a grudge against Liu Yan. War followed disaster, and the realm was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 此陛下親所聞見，得不深念哉！」

translations.literal: This Your Majesty personally heard and saw—you must reflect deeply!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty heard and saw this yourself—you must reflect on it deeply!"

sentences.zh: 紳繇是免。

translations.literal: Li Shen was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen was thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 逢吉怒，至寶歷三月赦書，不言左降官未量移者，以沮紳內徙。

translations.literal: Fengji was angry; when the Baoli third-month amnesty edict came, it did not mention demoted officials not yet eligible for transfer—to block Shen's inward move.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji was furious. When the third-month amnesty edict of the Baoli era was issued, it made no mention of demoted officials not yet eligible for transfer—a move intended to block Shen's return from exile.

sentences.zh: 處厚復奏：「逢吉緣紳一人而使近歲流斥皆不蒙澤，非所以廣恩於天下。」

translations.literal: Chuhou memorialized again: "For Fengji to use Shen alone to deny recent years' banished officials the amnesty—is not the way to spread grace under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou submitted another memorial: "Because of Shen alone, Fengji would deny every official banished in recent years the benefit of the amnesty. That is no way to spread grace throughout the realm."

sentences.zh: 帝悟，追改其條。

translations.literal: The emperor understood and retroactively amended that clause.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood and amended that clause retroactively.

sentences.zh: 進翰林承旨學士、兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted to Hanlin Chief Academician and Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin Chief Academician and Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 方天子荒暗，月視朝才三四。

translations.literal: Just then the Son of Heaven was dissolute and dim—he held court only three or four times a month.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Son of Heaven was dissolute and neglectful of duty, holding court only three or four times a month.

sentences.zh: 處厚入見，即自陳有罪，願前死以謝。

translations.literal: Chuhou entered audience and immediately declared himself guilty, wishing to die first as atonement.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou entered audience and immediately declared himself guilty, asking to die first as atonement.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何哉？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣昔為諫官，不能死爭，使先帝因畋與色而至不壽，於法應誅。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant formerly as remonstrance officer failed to argue to the death, allowing the late emperor through hunting and women to reach untimely death—by law I should be executed.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "When I served as a remonstrance officer, I failed to argue to the death and allowed the late emperor, through hunting and women, to die before his time. By law I deserve execution.

sentences.zh: 然所以不死者，陛下在春宮，十有五矣。

translations.literal: Yet the reason I did not die: Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace, already fifteen.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the reason I did not die was that Your Majesty was in the Eastern Palace, already fifteen years old.

sentences.zh: 今皇子方繈褓，臣不敢避死亡之誅。」

translations.literal: Now the prince is still in swaddling clothes—I dare not avoid the death penalty."
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince is still in swaddling clothes. I dare not avoid the penalty of death."

sentences.zh: 帝大感悟，賜錦彩以慰其意。

translations.literal: The emperor was deeply moved and gave brocade to comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply moved and granted him brocade to comfort him.

sentences.zh: 王廷湊之亂，帝嘆宰相不才，而使奸臣跋扈，處厚曰：「陛下有一裴度不能用，乃當饋而嘆，恨無蕭、曹，此馮唐所以謂漢文帝有頗、牧不能用也。」

translations.literal: In Wang Tingcou's rebellion the emperor sighed that chief ministers lacked talent, letting wicked ministers run rampant. Chuhou said: "Your Majesty has a Pei Du you cannot use—yet you sigh at the feast, lamenting you have no Xiao He or Cao Shen. This is why Feng Tang said Emperor Wen of Han had Li Mu and Lian Po but could not use them."
translations.idiomatic: During Wang Tingcou's rebellion the emperor lamented that his chief ministers lacked talent and allowed wicked ministers to run rampant. Chuhou said, "Your Majesty has a Pei Du whom you cannot use, yet you sigh over your meal, wishing you had men like Xiao He and Cao Shen. This is why Feng Tang said that Emperor Wen of Han had generals like Li Mu and Lian Po but could not employ them."

sentences.zh: 後禁中急變，文宗綏內難，猶豫未即下詔，處厚入，昌言曰：「《春秋》大義滅親，內惡必書，以明逆順；

translations.literal: Later an urgent crisis arose in the palace—Emperor Wenzong was settling internal strife, hesitating to issue an edict immediately. Chuhou entered and spoke forthrightly: "The Spring and Autumn Annals take as great principle extinguishing kin when necessary; inner evil must be recorded, to clarify rebellion from obedience;
translations.idiomatic: Later, when an urgent crisis broke out in the palace, Emperor Wenzong was suppressing an internal revolt but hesitated to issue an edict at once. Chuhou entered and spoke boldly: "The Spring and Autumn Annals enshrine the great principle that kin may be destroyed when duty requires it; inner evil must be recorded to make clear what is rebellion and what is loyalty;

sentences.zh: 正名討罪，何所避諱哉？」

translations.literal: rectify names and punish guilt—what is there to conceal?"
translations.idiomatic: To rectify names and punish guilt—what is there to conceal?"

sentences.zh: 遂奉教班諭。

translations.literal: He then received the command and issued proclamations in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He then received the imperial command and issued proclamations in turn.

sentences.zh: 是夕，號令及它儀矩不暇責有司，一出處厚，無違舊章者。

translations.literal: That evening, commands and other ritual rules—without time to hold the responsible offices accountable—all issued from Chuhou, none deviating from established regulations.
translations.idiomatic: That evening, commands and other ritual protocols were issued too quickly to hold the responsible offices to account; all came from Chuhou alone, and none departed from established precedent.

sentences.zh: 進拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，封靈昌郡公。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Chief Minister of the Chancellery and Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lingchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Chief Minister of the Chancellery and Secretariat, and enfeoffed as Duke of Lingchang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 堂史湯鉥數招權納財賂，處厚笑曰：「此半滑渙也。」

translations.literal: The hall clerk Tang Bo repeatedly usurped power and accepted bribes. Chuhou laughed and said: "This is half a Huà Huàn."
translations.idiomatic: The chancellery clerk Tang Bo repeatedly usurped authority and accepted bribes. Chuhou laughed and said, "This is half a Huà Huàn."

sentences.zh: 斥出之，相府肅然。

translations.literal: He expelled him, and the chancellor's office became solemn and orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He expelled him, and the chancellor's office became solemn and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 初，貞元時宰相齊抗奏罷州別駕及當為別駕者引處之朝。

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Zhenyuan era, Chief Minister Qi Kang memorialized to abolish provincial vice-prefects and to summon those who should serve as vice-prefects to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Zhenyuan era, Chief Minister Qi Kang had memorialized to abolish provincial vice-prefects and to summon to court those who were due to serve in that office.

sentences.zh: 元和後，兩河用兵，裨將立功得補東宮王府官，朱紫淆並，授受不綱。

translations.literal: After the Yuanhe era, with war in the Two He, staff officers who won merit were appointed as Eastern Palace and princely household officials; purple and red robes mingled indiscriminately, appointments and transfers lacked order.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanhe era, with war in the Two He, staff officers who won merit were appointed to Eastern Palace and princely household posts; purple and crimson robes mingled without distinction, and appointments and transfers fell into disorder.

sentences.zh: 處厚乃置六雄、十望、十緊等州，悉補別駕，由是流品澄別。

translations.literal: Chuhou then designated the Six Heroes, Ten Prominent, Ten Strategic, and other prefectures, all filling them with vice-prefects, thereby clarifying official ranks and distinctions.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou then designated the Six Heroes, Ten Prominent, Ten Strategic, and other prefectures, filling them all with vice-prefects, and thereby restored clarity to official ranks and distinctions.

sentences.zh: 帝雖自力機政，然驟信輕改，搖於浮論。

translations.literal: Although the emperor applied himself diligently to state affairs, he quickly believed and lightly changed course, swayed by idle talk.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor applied himself diligently to affairs of state, he was quick to believe and quick to change course, swayed by idle talk.

sentences.zh: 處厚嘗獨對曰：「陛下不以臣不肖，使待罪宰相，凡所奏可，中輒變易。

translations.literal: Chuhou once had a private audience and said: "Your Majesty, not deeming your servant unworthy, made me serve as chief minister bearing blame. Whatever I memorialized and received approval for is midway changed.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou once had a private audience and said, "Your Majesty, not deeming your servant unworthy, appointed me to serve as chief minister at peril of my life. Whatever I memorialized and Your Majesty approved is then altered midway.

sentences.zh: 自上心出邪，乃示臣不信；

translations.literal: If it comes from Your Majesty's own mind, is that not to show your servant that I am not trusted?
translations.idiomatic: If the change comes from Your Majesty's own mind, does that not show your servant that I am not trusted?

sentences.zh: 得於橫議邪，即臣何名執政？

translations.literal: If it comes from reckless talk, then what is your servant's title as one who governs?
translations.idiomatic: If it comes from reckless talk, then what title have I as one who governs?

sentences.zh: 且裴度元勛舊德，輔四朝，竇易直長厚忠實，經事先帝，陛下所宜親重委信之。

translations.literal: Moreover, Pei Du is a founding meritorious minister of old virtue who served four reigns; Dou Yizhi is generous, steady, loyal, and sincere and served the previous emperor. Your Majesty ought to hold them close, honor them, and entrust them with confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Pei Du is a founding minister of old virtue who served four reigns; Dou Yizhi is generous, steady, loyal, and sincere and served the previous emperor. Your Majesty ought to hold them close, honor them, and place your trust in them.

sentences.zh: 臣乃陛下自擢，今言不見納，宜先罷。」

translations.literal: Your servant was personally elevated by Your Majesty. If my words are not heeded, I ought to be dismissed first."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant was personally elevated by Your Majesty. If my words are not heeded, I ought to be dismissed first."

sentences.zh: 即趨下頓首，帝矍然曰：「何至是？

translations.literal: He immediately hurried down and kowtowed. The emperor started and said: "How could it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: He immediately hurried down and kowtowed. The emperor started and said, "How could it come to this?

sentences.zh: 卿之忠力，朕自知之，安可遽辭以重吾不德？」

translations.literal: Your loyalty and strength—I know them myself. How can you abruptly resign and redouble my lack of virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty and strength—I know them myself. How can you abruptly resign and redouble my lack of virtue?"

sentences.zh: 處厚趨出，帝復召問所欲言，乃對：「近君子，遠小人，始可為治。」

translations.literal: Chuhou hurried out. The emperor summoned him again and asked what he wished to say. He replied: "Draw near to gentlemen and keep petty men at a distance—only then may good government begin."
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou hurried out. The emperor summoned him again and asked what he wished to say. He replied, "Draw near to gentlemen and keep petty men at a distance—only then may good government begin."

sentences.zh: 諄復數百言。

translations.literal: He earnestly expounded for several hundred more words.
translations.idiomatic: He earnestly expounded for several hundred more words.

sentences.zh: 又言：「裴度忠，可久任。」

translations.literal: He added: "Pei Du is loyal and may be long entrusted with office."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Pei Du is loyal and may be long entrusted with office."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 自是無復橫議者。

translations.literal: From then on there were no more reckless talkers.
translations.idiomatic: From then on there were no more reckless talkers.

sentences.zh: 時李同捷叛，詔諸軍進討。

translations.literal: At that time Li Tongjie rebelled, and an edict ordered the various armies to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Li Tongjie rebelled, and an edict ordered the various armies to advance and attack.

sentences.zh: 魏博史憲誠懷向背，裴度待以不疑。

translations.literal: Shi Xiancheng of Weibo wavered between loyalty and defection; Pei Du treated him without suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiancheng of Weibo wavered between loyalty and defection; Pei Du treated him without suspicion.

sentences.zh: 憲誠遣吏白事中書，處厚召語曰：「晉公以百口保爾帥於天子，我則不然，正須所為，以邦法從事耳。」

translations.literal: Xiancheng sent a clerk to report affairs at the Chancellery. Chuhou summoned and told him: "The Duke of Jin pledges his hundred mouths to vouch for your commander to the Son of Heaven. I am not so. I need only act according to what is right and deal with you under state law."
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng sent a clerk to report affairs at the Chancellery. Chuhou summoned him and said, "The Duke of Jin pledges the lives of his entire household to vouch for your commander to the Son of Heaven. I am not so. I need only do what is right and deal with you according to state law."

sentences.zh: 憲誠懼，不敢貳，卒有功。

translations.literal: Xiancheng was afraid, dared not waver, and in the end achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng was afraid, dared not waver, and in the end achieved merit.

sentences.zh: 李載義數破滄、鎮兵，皆刳剔以獻，處厚戒之，前後完活數百千人。

translations.literal: Li Zaiyi repeatedly defeated Cangzhou and Zhenzhou troops and had them gutted and flayed for presentation. Chuhou admonished him, and in all several hundred to a thousand people were spared alive.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zaiyi repeatedly defeated the armies of Cangzhou and Zhenzhou and had the captives gutted and flayed for presentation. Chuhou admonished him, and in all several hundred to a thousand people were spared alive.

sentences.zh: 大和二年，方奏事，暴疾，仆香案前，帝命中人翼扶之，輿還第，一昔薨，年五十六，贈司空。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dahe, while reporting on affairs, he suddenly fell ill, collapsed before the incense stand, the emperor ordered eunuchs to support him on either side, had him carried back to his residence, and died that same night at age fifty-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Dahe, while reporting on affairs, he suddenly fell ill and collapsed before the incense stand. The emperor ordered eunuchs to support him on either side, had him carried back to his residence, and he died that same night at age fifty-six. He was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 處厚姿狀如甚懦者，居家亦循易，至廷爭，嶷然不可回奪。

translations.literal: Chuhou's bearing and appearance were like that of a very timid man; at home too he was meek and mild. Yet when disputing matters at court, he stood firm and immovable.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou's bearing and appearance were like that of a very timid man; at home too he was meek and mild. Yet when disputing matters at court, he stood firm and could not be turned aside.

sentences.zh: 剛於禦吏，百僚謁事，畏惕未嘗敢及以私。

translations.literal: He was stern in controlling clerks. When officials came on business, in fear and caution they never dared bring up private matters.
translations.idiomatic: He was stern in controlling clerks. When officials came on business, in fear and caution they never dared bring up private matters.

sentences.zh: 推擇官材，往往棄瑕錄善，時亦譏其太廣。

translations.literal: In recommending and selecting talent for office, he often overlooked flaws and recorded virtues; at times he was criticized for being too broad.
translations.idiomatic: In recommending and selecting talent for office, he often overlooked flaws and recorded virtues; at times he was criticized for being too broad.

sentences.zh: 性嗜學，家書讎正至萬卷。

translations.literal: By nature he loved learning; his family library, collated and corrected, reached ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved learning; his family library, collated and corrected, reached ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 為拾遺時，撰《德宗實錄》。

translations.literal: When he was Reminder, he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.
translations.idiomatic: When he served as Reminder, he compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Dezong.

sentences.zh: 後又與路隋共次《憲宗實錄》，詔分日入直，創具凡例，未及成而終。

translations.literal: Later he joined Lu Sui in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong. An edict ordered them to enter duty on alternating days; they drafted the general principles but before completion he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Lu Sui in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Xianzong. An edict ordered them to enter duty on alternating days; they drafted the general principles, but before the work was finished he died.

sentences.zh: 本名淳，避憲宗諱，改今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Chun; to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Xianzong, he changed to his present name.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Chun; to avoid the taboo name of Emperor Xianzong, he changed to his present name.

sentences.zh: 路隋，字南式，其先出陽平。

translations.literal: Lu Sui, styled Nanshi, his ancestors came from Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Sui, styled Nanshi, traced his descent to Yangping.

sentences.zh: 父泌，字安期，通《五經》，端亮寡言，以孝悌聞。

translations.literal: His father Bi, styled Anqi, mastered the Five Classics, was upright and bright and sparing of words, and was known for filial piety and brotherly respect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi, styled Anqi, mastered the Five Classics, was upright and bright and sparing of words, and was known for filial piety and brotherly respect.

sentences.zh: 建中末，為長安尉。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianzhong era, he served as warden of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Jianzhong era, he served as warden of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，棄妻子奔行在，扈狩梁州，排亂軍以出，再中流矢，裂裳濡血。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong went out to Fengtian, he abandoned wife and children and fled to the mobile court, escorting the hunt at Liangzhou, breaking through disorderly troops to get out, was twice struck by stray arrows, his robe torn and soaked with blood.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong went out to Fengtian, he abandoned wife and children and fled to the mobile court, escorting the imperial hunt at Liangzhou, breaking through disorderly troops to get out. He was twice struck by stray arrows, his robe torn and soaked with blood.

sentences.zh: 以策說渾瑊，召置幕府。

translations.literal: With his stratagem he persuaded Hun Zhen and was summoned to be placed in his staff headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: With his stratagem he persuaded Hun Zhen and was summoned to serve on his staff.

sentences.zh: 東討李懷光，奏署副元帥判官。

translations.literal: Campaigning east against Li Huaiguang, he was memorialized and appointed deputy commander staff judge.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning east against Li Huaiguang, he was memorialized and appointed staff judge to the deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 從瑊會盟平涼，為虜所執，死焉。

translations.literal: Following Zhen to the alliance meeting at Pingliang, he was seized by the barbarians and died there.
translations.idiomatic: Following Zhen to the alliance meeting at Pingliang, he was seized by the barbarians and died there.

sentences.zh: 時隋嬰孺，以恩授八品官。

translations.literal: At that time Sui was an infant; by grace he was granted an eighth-rank office.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Sui was an infant; by grace he was granted an eighth-rank office.

sentences.zh: 逮長，知父執虜中，日夜號泣，坐必西向，不食肉。

translations.literal: When he grew up, knowing his father was held among the barbarians, he wept day and night, when seated always faced west, and ate no meat.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up, knowing his father was held captive among the barbarians, he wept day and night, always faced west when seated, and ate no meat.

sentences.zh: 母告以貌類泌者，終身不引鏡。

translations.literal: When his mother told him his appearance resembled Bi's, he never looked in a mirror for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother told him his appearance resembled Bi's, he never looked in a mirror for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，吐蕃請和，隋三上疏宜許，不報。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, Tibet requested peace; Sui three times memorialized that it should be granted, with no response.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Zhenyuan era, Tibet requested peace; Sui three times memorialized that it should be granted, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，授潤州參軍事。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant military adjutant of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed assistant military adjutant of Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李锜欲困辱之，使知市事，隋怡然坐肆，不為屈。

translations.literal: Li Qi wished to humiliate him and made him overseer of market affairs; Sui serenely sat at the shop, unbowed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qi wished to humiliate him and made him overseer of market affairs; Sui serenely sat at the shop, unbowed.

sentences.zh: 韋夏卿高其節，辟置東都幕府。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaqing held his integrity in high esteem and recruited him to the Eastern Capital staff.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing held his integrity in high esteem and recruited him to the Eastern Capital staff.

sentences.zh: 元和中，吐蕃款塞，隋五上疏請脩好，冀得泌還。

translations.literal: During the Yuanhe era, Tibet came in friendship to the frontier; Sui five times memorialized requesting restored good relations, hoping to get Bi back.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era, Tibet came in friendship to the frontier; Sui five times memorialized requesting restored good relations, hoping to get Bi back.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 遣祠部郎中徐復報聘，而泌以喪至，帝湣惻，贈絳州刺史，官為治喪。

translations.literal: Bureau Director of the Court of Sacrifices Xu Fu was dispatched on a return mission, and Bi arrived as a corpse; the emperor was moved to pity, posthumously enfeoffed him as prefect of Jiangzhou, and officials arranged his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director of the Court of Sacrifices Xu Fu was dispatched on a return mission, and Bi arrived as a corpse. The emperor was moved to pity, posthumously enfeoffed him as Prefect of Jiang Prefecture, and officials arranged his funeral.

sentences.zh: 服除，擢隋左補闕、史館脩撰，以鯁亮稱。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Sui was promoted to Left Supplements Censor and Historiography Compiler, famed for blunt integrity.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Sui was promoted to Left Supplements Censor and Historiography Compiler, famed for blunt integrity.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，與韋處厚並擢侍講學士，再遷中書舍人、翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong ascended, he and Wei Chuhou were both promoted to Palace Lecturer and Erudite, then twice transferred to Secretariat Drafting Official and Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended, he and Wei Chuhou were both promoted to Palace Lecturer and Erudite, then twice transferred to Secretariat Drafting Official and Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 每除制出，以金幣來謝者，隋卻之曰：「公事而當私貺邪？」

translations.literal: Whenever appointment edicts were issued, those who came with gold and silk to thank him—Sui refused and said: "Is this public business, yet you would offer private gifts?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever appointment edicts were issued, those who came with gold and silk to thank him—Sui refused and said, "Is this public business, yet you would offer private gifts?"

sentences.zh: 進承旨學士，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Lead Academician and transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Lead Academician and transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 文宗嗣位，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事，監脩國史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong succeeded, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Chief Minister, and superintendent of compiling the National History.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong succeeded, he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat, Co-Chief Minister, and superintendent of compiling the National History.

sentences.zh: 初，韓愈撰《順宗實錄》，書禁中事為切直，宦豎不喜，訾其非實，帝詔隋刊正。

translations.literal: Earlier, Han Yu compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong; in recording palace affairs his language was sharp and direct. The eunuch minions disliked it and denounced it as untrue; the emperor ordered Sui to revise and correct it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Yu compiled the Veritable Records of Emperor Shunzong; in recording palace affairs his language was sharp and direct. The eunuch minions disliked it and denounced it as untrue; the emperor ordered Sui to revise and correct it.

sentences.zh: 隋建言：「衛尉卿周居巢、諫議大夫王彥威、給事中李固言、史官蘇景胤皆上言改脩非是。

translations.literal: Sui submitted: "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhou Juchao, Remonstrating Advisor Wang Yanwei, Palace Aide Li Guyin, and historiographer Su Jingyin all memorialized that revising it was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Sui submitted: "Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Zhou Juchao, Remonstrating Advisor Wang Yanwei, Palace Aide Li Guyin, and historiographer Su Jingyin all memorialized that revising it was wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫史冊者，褒勸所在，匹夫美惡尚不可誣，況人君乎？

translations.literal: Histories are where praise and encouragement reside; even a common man's good and evil cannot be falsified—how much more a ruler?
translations.idiomatic: Histories are where praise and encouragement reside; even a common man's good and evil cannot be falsified—how much more a ruler?

sentences.zh: 議者至引雋不疑、第五倫為比，以蔽聰明。

translations.literal: Those arguing even cited Jun Buyi and Di Wu Lun as parallels, to obscure clear judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Those arguing even cited Jun Buyi and Di Wu Lun as parallels, to obscure clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 臣宗閔、臣僧孺謂史官李漢、蔣系皆愈之婿，不可參撰，俾臣得下筆。

translations.literal: Your ministers Zongmin and Sengru say the historiographers Li Han and Jiang Xi are both Han Yu's sons-in-law and may not participate in compilation, enabling your servant to put brush to paper.
translations.idiomatic: Your ministers Zongmin and Sengru say the historiographers Li Han and Jiang Xi are both Han Yu's sons-in-law and may not participate in compilation, enabling your servant to put brush to paper.

sentences.zh: 臣謂不然。

translations.literal: Your servant holds this is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds this is not so.

sentences.zh: 且愈所書已非自出，元和以來，相循逮今。

translations.literal: Moreover, what Han Yu wrote was not of his own invention; since the Yuanhe era it has been handed down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, what Han Yu wrote was not of his own invention; since the Yuanhe era it has been handed down to the present.

sentences.zh: 雖漢等以嫌，無害公誼。

translations.literal: Though Han and the others have a connection by marriage, this does no harm to public principle.
translations.idiomatic: Though Han and the others have a connection by marriage, this does no harm to public principle.

sentences.zh: 請條示甚謬誤者，付史官刊定。」

translations.literal: Please itemize what is grossly erroneous and hand it to the historiographers to revise and fix."
translations.idiomatic: Please itemize what is grossly erroneous and hand it to the historiographers to revise and fix."

sentences.zh: 有詔擿貞元、永貞間數事為失實，餘不復改，漢等亦不罷。

translations.literal: An edict singled out several matters between the Zhenyuan and Yongzhen eras as inaccurate; the rest was not further changed, and Han and the others were not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict singled out several matters between the Zhenyuan and Yongzhen eras as inaccurate; the rest was not further changed, and Han and the others were not dismissed.

sentences.zh: 進門下侍郎、弘文館大學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 久之，辭疾，不聽，冊拜太子太師。

translations.literal: After a long while he submitted illness and asked to retire; this was not granted, and he was invested by edict as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he submitted illness and asked to retire; this was not granted, and he was invested by edict as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 明年，李德裕貶袁州長史，不署奏，為鄭註所忌，乃檢校尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事、鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: The next year, when Li Deyu was demoted to secretary of Yuanzhou and Sui refused to sign the memorial, Zheng Zhu bore a grudge against him; he was then made provisional Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Chief Minister, and military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when Li Deyu was demoted to secretary of Yuan Prefecture and Sui refused to sign the memorial, Zheng Zhu bore a grudge against him; he was then made provisional Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Chief Minister, and military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 道病卒，年六十。

translations.literal: He died of illness on the road at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness on the road at age sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Upright.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Upright.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：綰以德服人，而人自化，可謂賢矣。

translations.literal: The eulogist says: Wan won people through virtue, and they reformed themselves—he may be called worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogist says: Wan won people through virtue, and they reformed themselves—he may be called worthy.

sentences.zh: 其論議渾大，雖古王佐無以加。

translations.literal: His discourse was vast and comprehensive; even ancient prime counselors could not surpass it.
translations.idiomatic: His discourse was vast and comprehensive; even ancient prime counselors could not surpass it.

sentences.zh: 祐甫發正己隱情，渾策吐蕃必叛，伐謀知幾，君子哉！

translations.literal: Youfu exposed Zhengji's hidden designs; Hun foresaw that Tibet would surely rebel—foiling plots and discerning the moment, true gentlemen!
translations.idiomatic: Youfu exposed Zhengji's hidden designs; Hun foresaw that Tibet would surely rebel—foiling plots and discerning the moment, true gentlemen!

sentences.zh: 處厚事穆、敬、文三宗，主皆弗類，而一納以忠，寧不謂以堯事君者邪？

translations.literal: Chuhou served Emperors Muzong, Jingzong, and Wenzong—masters none alike—yet served each with single-minded loyalty. Is he not one who served his lord as Yao would?
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou served Emperors Muzong, Jingzong, and Wenzong—masters none alike—yet served each with single-minded loyalty. Is he not one who served his lord as Yao would?

sentences.zh: 隋輔政十年，歷牛、李、訓、註用事，無所迎將，善保位哉！

translations.literal: Sui assisted government for ten years, through the ascendancies of the Niu, Li, Xun, and Zhu factions—never courting or accommodating any—and yet preserved his position well!
translations.idiomatic: Sui assisted government for ten years, through the ascendancies of the Niu, Li, Xun, and Zhu factions—never courting or accommodating any—and yet preserved his position well!
